name: Common carotid artery
function: Main arterial trunk of the head and neck; gives no branches in the neck and bifurcates at C4 (upper border of thyroid cartilage) into internal and external carotid arteries.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Right: brachiocephalic trunk behind the right sternoclavicular joint. Left: directly from the aortic arch (so it has a short thoracic course).

details.label: Course
details.value: Ascends in the carotid sheath with the internal jugular vein (lateral) and vagus nerve (posterior, between the two vessels), deep to SCM, to the upper border of the thyroid cartilage (C4).

details.label: Branches
details.value: None in the neck; terminates as internal and external carotid arteries.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Entire head and neck via its terminal branches.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Ansa cervicalis on the sheath; sympathetic trunk posterior (outside the sheath); omohyoid crosses it at C6, where it can be compressed against the carotid tubercle (Chassaignac) of C6.

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Right common carotid artery (from the brachiocephalic trunk behind the right sternoclavicular joint); left common carotid artery (directly from the aortic arch, so it has a thoracic part). Each ends at the carotid bifurcation as the internal carotid artery (to brain and orbit) and external carotid artery (to face, scalp and neck).

pearl: Palpate the carotid pulse at the thyroid cartilage, medial to SCM, one side at a time. Bruit with TIA/amaurosis fugax: carotid duplex; symptomatic 70-99% stenosis gets endarterectomy within 2 weeks. For IJ central lines the vein lies lateral to the pulse.

name: Carotid bifurcation (carotid sinus and carotid body)
function: Division of the common carotid at C4 (upper border of thyroid cartilage). The carotid sinus is a baroreceptor dilatation; the carotid body is a chemoreceptor.

details.label: Level
details.value: C4, upper border of thyroid cartilage, within the carotid triangle.

details.label: Carotid sinus
details.value: Dilatation at the origin of the internal carotid; baroreceptors sense stretch (blood pressure) via the carotid sinus nerve (Hering), a branch of CN IX, to the medulla.

details.label: Carotid body
details.value: Small chemoreceptor at the bifurcation; senses PO2, PCO2 and pH; afferents via CN IX (and X).

details.label: Relations
details.value: Hypoglossal nerve loops across both carotids just above the bifurcation; the internal jugular vein lies lateral. Atherosclerotic plaque forms preferentially here.

pearl: Carotid endarterectomy for symptomatic 70-99% stenosis; carotid sinus massage or a tight collar can cause bradycardia/syncope (carotid sinus hypersensitivity). Carotid body tumor (paraganglioma): painless pulsatile neck mass mobile side-to-side but not vertically, splaying ICA/ECA (lyre sign).

name: Internal carotid artery
function: Supplies the brain, eye and orbit. Has no branches in the neck, which distinguishes it from the external carotid.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Carotid bifurcation at C4; initially posterolateral to the external carotid, then medial to it as it ascends.

details.label: Course
details.value: Cervical part: ascends in carotid sheath to the carotid canal. Petrous part: through temporal bone. Cavernous part: S-shaped siphon in the cavernous sinus beside CN VI. Cerebral part: medial to anterior clinoid.

details.label: Branches
details.value: None in the neck. Petrous part: caroticotympanic artery. Cavernous part: meningohypophyseal trunk (tentorial, dorsal meningeal and inferior hypophyseal branches) and the inferolateral trunk (artery to the inferior cavernous sinus). Cerebral part: ophthalmic, superior hypophyseal, posterior communicating and anterior choroidal arteries, then the terminal anterior and middle cerebral arteries.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Anterior circulation of the brain (anterior and middle cerebral territories), eye, orbit, forehead and nose.

details.label: Relations
details.value: CN IX, X, XI, XII and the sympathetic plexus lie near its cervical course; the styloid process and its muscles separate it (deep) from the external carotid and parotid (superficial).

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Cervical part (bifurcation to carotid canal; no branches). Petrous part (in the carotid canal of the temporal bone; caroticotympanic artery, artery of pterygoid canal). Cavernous part (in the cavernous sinus; meningohypophyseal trunk with tentorial, dorsal meningeal and inferior hypophyseal branches, artery to inferior cavernous sinus/inferolateral trunk, recurrent artery of foramen lacerum, branches to foramen rotundum, ovale and spinosum, meningeal and cavernous branches). Cerebral part (above the anterior clinoid; ophthalmic, superior hypophyseal, posterior communicating and anterior choroidal arteries, ending as anterior and middle cerebral arteries).

pearl: Carotid dissection (trauma, chiropractic manipulation, fibromuscular dysplasia): unilateral neck pain, partial Horner syndrome (ptosis, miosis, no anhidrosis) and ipsilateral stroke or amaurosis fugax; diagnose with CT/MR angiography, treat with antithrombotics.

name: External carotid artery
function: Supplies the face, scalp, neck, oral and nasal cavities and the dura via eight branches; terminates in the parotid as maxillary and superficial temporal arteries.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Carotid bifurcation at C4, anteromedial to the internal carotid.

details.label: Course
details.value: Ascends in the carotid triangle, passes deep to the posterior belly of digastric and stylohyoid, enters the parotid gland and ends behind the neck of the mandible.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Anterior: superior thyroid, lingual, facial. Medial: ascending pharyngeal. Posterior: occipital, posterior auricular. Terminal: maxillary, superficial temporal (mnemonic: Some Anatomists Like Freaking Out Poor Medical Students).

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Thyroid, larynx, tongue, face, pharynx, scalp, ear, meninges, jaws and nasal cavity.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Hypoglossal nerve crosses it laterally just above the bifurcation; facial nerve branches lie superficial to it within the parotid.

pearl: ECA-ICA anastomoses (angular-ophthalmic, facial-ethmoidal) can provide collateral flow in internal carotid occlusion; ECA branches are the targets of embolization for refractory epistaxis.

name: Superior thyroid artery (with superior laryngeal artery)
function: First anterior branch of the external carotid; supplies the upper pole of the thyroid gland and, via the superior laryngeal artery, the larynx.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Anterior surface of the external carotid just above the bifurcation (occasionally from the common carotid).

details.label: Course
details.value: Runs downward and forward with the external laryngeal nerve, deep to the infrahyoid muscles, to the upper pole of the thyroid lobe.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Superior laryngeal artery (pierces thyrohyoid membrane with the internal laryngeal nerve), infrahyoid, sternocleidomastoid, cricothyroid and glandular branches.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Upper pole of the thyroid; larynx via the superior laryngeal and cricothyroid arteries (the intrinsic laryngeal muscles, including cricothyroid, are shared with the inferior thyroid artery); infrahyoid muscles (sternohyoid, sternothyroid, thyrohyoid, omohyoid); SCM; inferior pharyngeal constrictor.

details.label: Relations
details.value: External laryngeal nerve runs with it, diverging just before the upper pole; the artery is ligated close to the gland to spare the nerve.

pearl: Thyroidectomy: ligate the superior thyroid artery close to the gland to avoid the external laryngeal nerve (cricothyroid); injury causes loss of high-pitch voice and vocal fatigue.

name: Ascending pharyngeal artery
function: Small medial branch of the external carotid that ascends on the pharynx to supply the pharyngeal wall, palatine tonsil, middle ear and posterior cranial fossa dura.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Medial (deep) surface of the external carotid near its origin; smallest branch.

details.label: Course
details.value: Ascends between the internal carotid artery and the lateral pharyngeal wall to the skull base.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Pharyngeal and tonsillar branches, prevertebral (muscular) branches, inferior tympanic artery (through the tympanic canaliculus), and posterior meningeal branches (via the jugular foramen and condylar canal).

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Pharynx, palatine tonsil, soft palate, middle ear, posterior fossa meninges, prevertebral muscles; main feeder of glomus jugulare/tympanicum paragangliomas.

pearl: Contributes to tonsillar supply with the tonsillar branch of the facial artery. Post-tonsillectomy hemorrhage is primary (<24 h, surgical) or secondary (5-10 days, eschar slough): secure airway, IV access, return to OR if active.

name: Lingual artery
function: Second anterior branch of the external carotid; principal artery of the tongue, floor of the mouth and sublingual gland.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Anterior surface of the external carotid at the level of the tip of the greater horn of the hyoid (between superior thyroid and facial); may share a linguofacial trunk with the facial artery.

details.label: Course
details.value: Loops upward (the loop is crossed laterally by the hypoglossal nerve), passes deep to hyoglossus, then runs forward beneath the tongue as the deep lingual artery.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Suprahyoid, dorsal lingual, sublingual and deep lingual arteries.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Intrinsic tongue muscles (deep lingual); extrinsic tongue muscles, sublingual gland, floor of mouth, mylohyoid and geniohyoid (sublingual); palatine tonsil and pharyngeal constrictors (dorsal lingual); hyoid and infrahyoid muscles, omohyoid and sternohyoid (suprahyoid/hyoid branch).

details.label: Relations
details.value: Hyoglossus separates the artery (deep) from the hypoglossal nerve and its vena comitans / deep lingual vein (superficial); the artery is exposed for ligation by dividing hyoglossus.

pearl: Deep lingual arteries do not anastomose across the midline septum, so a midline tongue incision is relatively bloodless; a lateral tongue laceration or cancer resection can bleed profusely.

name: Facial artery
function: Major artery of the face; tortuous course from the neck across the mandible to the medial canthus, supplying the lips, cheek, nose and submandibular gland.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Anterior surface of the external carotid just above the lingual artery, in the carotid triangle.

details.label: Course
details.value: Deep to digastric and stylohyoid, grooves the submandibular gland, then curls over the lower border of the mandible at the anterior edge of masseter and runs tortuously to the angle of the mouth, side of the nose and medial canthus.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Cervical: ascending palatine, tonsillar, glandular, submental. Facial: inferior labial, superior labial, lateral nasal, angular (terminal).

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Submandibular gland; palatine tonsil, soft palate muscles and pharyngeal wall (ascending palatine, tonsillar); anterior belly of digastric, mylohyoid, genioglossus/hyoglossus and platysma (submental); stylohyoid; masseter and medial pterygoid; buccinator and the muscles of facial expression of the lips, nose and cheek (labial, lateral nasal, angular); orbicularis oculi (angular, with the superficial temporal artery); anastomoses with the ophthalmic artery at the medial canthus.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Marginal mandibular branch of CN VII crosses it superficially at the mandible; facial vein lies posterior to the artery and runs straighter.

pearl: Facial pulse is felt where the artery crosses the mandible at the anterior border of masseter; lacerations here bleed briskly and the marginal mandibular nerve is at risk in submandibular incisions.

name: Occipital artery
function: Posterior branch of the external carotid that supplies the posterior scalp, SCM and posterior neck muscles.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Posterior surface of the external carotid opposite the facial artery, crossed by the hypoglossal nerve at its origin.

details.label: Course
details.value: Runs backward along the lower border of the posterior belly of digastric, deep to the mastoid process (occipital groove), then pierces the fascia between trapezius and SCM to ascend the scalp with the greater occipital nerve.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Sternocleidomastoid (2), mastoid, auricular, meningeal, descending (anastomoses with deep cervical and vertebral) and terminal occipital branches.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Posterior scalp (occipitalis, descending branch), SCM, posterior belly of digastric and stylohyoid, rectus capitis lateralis and deep posterior neck muscles, mastoid and posterior fossa dura (mastoid and meningeal branches); descending branch anastomoses with the deep cervical artery (collateral to the vertebral).

pearl: Occipital artery runs with the greater occipital nerve; it is a landmark for occipital nerve block in occipital neuralgia. Its descending branch gives collateral flow in vertebral artery occlusion.

name: Posterior auricular artery
function: Small posterior branch of the external carotid supplying the auricle, scalp behind the ear, and (via the stylomastoid artery) the facial nerve and middle ear.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Posterior surface of the external carotid above the posterior belly of digastric, deep to the parotid.

details.label: Course
details.value: Ascends on the styloid process deep to the parotid, then between the auricle and the mastoid process.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Stylomastoid artery (enters the stylomastoid foramen with CN VII; gives posterior tympanic and stapedial branches), auricular branch, occipital branch and muscular branches.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Auricle and auricular muscles, scalp behind the ear (occipitalis), SCM, posterior belly of digastric, parotid, facial nerve in its canal, stapedius, tympanic cavity and mastoid air cells.

pearl: Its stylomastoid branch runs with CN VII through the stylomastoid foramen. Bell palsy (HSV-associated nerve edema in the facial canal): prednisone within 72 h, add valacyclovir if severe, and protect the eye.

name: Maxillary artery
function: Larger terminal branch of the external carotid; supplies the deep face, jaws, teeth, dura, nasal cavity and palate through three parts (mandibular, pterygoid, pterygopalatine).

details.label: Origin
details.value: Terminal branch of the external carotid behind the neck of the mandible within the parotid.

details.label: Course
details.value: 1st (mandibular) part: between neck of mandible and sphenomandibular ligament. 2nd (pterygoid) part: on lateral pterygoid in the infratemporal fossa. 3rd part: enters the pterygopalatine fossa via the pterygomaxillary fissure.

details.label: Branches
details.value: 1st: deep auricular, anterior tympanic, middle meningeal (via foramen spinosum), accessory meningeal, inferior alveolar. 2nd: deep temporal, pterygoid, masseteric, buccal. 3rd: posterior superior alveolar, infraorbital, descending palatine, artery of pterygoid canal, pharyngeal, sphenopalatine.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Mandible and lower teeth (inferior alveolar), maxilla and upper teeth (superior alveolar), muscles of mastication (deep temporal, masseteric, pterygoid branches), buccinator (buccal), dura (middle and accessory meningeal), external and middle ear including tensor tympani and stapedius (deep auricular, anterior tympanic, superior tympanic), nasal cavity (sphenopalatine), hard and soft palate and tonsil (descending/greater and lesser palatine).

details.label: Relations
details.value: Runs with the mandibular nerve branches; the 2nd part lies superficial or deep to lateral pterygoid.

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Mandibular (1st) part, behind the neck of the mandible: deep auricular, anterior tympanic, middle meningeal, accessory meningeal, inferior alveolar (with mylohyoid branch). Pterygoid (2nd) part, on or deep to lateral pterygoid: anterior and posterior deep temporal, masseteric, medial and lateral pterygoid, buccal. Pterygopalatine (3rd) part, in the pterygopalatine fossa: posterior superior alveolar, infraorbital (with middle and anterior superior alveolar), descending palatine (greater and lesser palatine), artery of pterygoid canal, pharyngeal, sphenopalatine (posterior lateral nasal and posterior septal branches).

pearl: Middle meningeal artery torn by a pterion fracture causes epidural hematoma (lucid interval, lens-shaped bleed). Sphenopalatine artery is the target for embolization or ligation in intractable posterior epistaxis.

name: Superficial temporal artery
function: Smaller terminal branch of the external carotid; supplies the temporal scalp, forehead, parotid and ear, and is the most palpable scalp artery.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Terminal branch of the external carotid within the parotid gland behind the neck of the mandible.

details.label: Course
details.value: Ascends in front of the tragus with the auriculotemporal nerve, crosses the posterior root of the zygomatic arch and divides into frontal and parietal branches on the temporal fascia.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Transverse facial, middle temporal, zygomatico-orbital, anterior auricular, frontal and parietal branches.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Parotid, TMJ, auricle and auricular muscles (parietal branch), masseter (transverse facial), temporalis (middle temporal), orbicularis oculi and corrugator supercilii (zygomatic branches), frontalis and the lateral scalp and forehead (frontal branch).

details.label: Relations
details.value: Auriculotemporal nerve runs posterior to the artery; temporal branches of CN VII cross the zygomatic arch anterior to it.

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Frontal (anterior) branch: runs forward over the temple to the forehead, anastomoses with supraorbital and supratrochlear arteries. Parietal (posterior) branch: runs up and back over the parietal scalp, anastomoses with posterior auricular and occipital arteries. Collateral branches before the division: transverse facial, middle temporal, zygomatico-orbital and anterior auricular arteries.

pearl: Giant cell (temporal) arteritis: age >50, headache, jaw claudication, tender pulseless STA, high ESR; start high-dose steroids immediately to prevent blindness, then temporal artery biopsy.

name: Middle meningeal artery
function: Largest meningeal artery; supplies the dura and calvarial bone of the middle cranial fossa. Its anterior branch runs beneath the pterion, the thinnest part of the skull.

details.label: Origin
details.value: First (mandibular) part of the maxillary artery in the infratemporal fossa.

details.label: Course
details.value: Passes between the two roots of the auriculotemporal nerve, enters the skull through the foramen spinosum, then runs laterally and forward on the floor of the middle fossa before dividing into frontal (anterior) and parietal (posterior) branches grooving the inner skull.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Frontal (anterior) branch deep to the pterion; parietal (posterior) branch; superficial petrosal branch (runs with the greater petrosal nerve to the facial nerve); superior tympanic branch (to tensor tympani); orbital anastomotic branch to the lacrimal artery (recurrent meningeal).

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Dura mater and bone of the middle cranial fossa and calvaria (not the brain); tensor tympani (superior tympanic branch) and stapedius; facial nerve in the facial canal (superficial petrosal branch).

details.label: Relations
details.value: Lies in the outer periosteal (endosteal) layer of the dura, grooving the inner table of the skull; the cranial epidural space is only a potential space, made real when the artery tears. Accompanied by middle meningeal veins and the meningeal branch of V3.

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Frontal (anterior) branch: crosses the greater wing of the sphenoid deep to the pterion, supplies anterior dura and calvaria. Parietal (posterior) branch: curves back over the squamous temporal and parietal bone, supplies posterior dura and calvaria.

pearl: Epidural hematoma: temporal bone fracture at the pterion tears the MMA; lucid interval then rapid deterioration, lens-shaped (biconvex) hematoma on CT that does not cross sutures; emergent craniotomy.

name: Inferior alveolar artery
function: Branch of the first part of the maxillary artery that runs in the mandibular canal with the inferior alveolar nerve to supply the mandible, lower teeth, chin and lower lip.

details.label: Origin
details.value: First (mandibular) part of the maxillary artery, in the infratemporal fossa.

details.label: Course
details.value: Descends with the inferior alveolar nerve (V3) behind the lingual nerve, enters the mandibular foramen on the medial ramus, runs forward in the mandibular canal and exits the mental foramen as the mental artery.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Lingual branch (near its origin, to the tongue mucosa), mylohyoid branch (before entering the canal, with the nerve to mylohyoid), dental branches, incisive branch, mental branch (exits the mental foramen).

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Mandible, lower teeth and gingiva, mylohyoid, chin and lower lip skin.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Lingual nerve lies anterior and medial to the inferior alveolar neurovascular bundle above the mandibular foramen.

pearl: Inferior alveolar nerve block: anesthetic is deposited near the mandibular foramen medial to the ramus; aspirate first because intravascular injection into the artery or the nearby pterygoid plexus is common.

name: Sphenopalatine artery
function: Terminal branch of the maxillary artery and the principal artery of the nasal cavity; the usual source of posterior epistaxis.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Third (pterygopalatine) part of the maxillary artery in the pterygopalatine fossa.

details.label: Course
details.value: Passes through the sphenopalatine foramen with the nasopalatine nerve into the posterior nasal cavity at the posterior end of the middle turbinate.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Posterior lateral nasal arteries (to turbinates and sinuses) and posterior septal branches (nasopalatine artery, running down the septum to the incisive canal).

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Lateral nasal wall, turbinates, nasal septum, paranasal sinuses; contributes to Kiesselbach plexus.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Enters the nose just behind the posterior end of the middle turbinate, the landmark for endoscopic sphenopalatine artery ligation.

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Posterior lateral nasal branches (to the conchae, meatuses and sinuses of the lateral wall); posterior septal branches (across the sphenoid face to the septum, anastomosing with the greater palatine artery in the incisive canal).

pearl: Posterior epistaxis (older, hypertensive, anticoagulated patients) usually arises from the sphenopalatine artery: blood runs down the throat, anterior packing fails, and it needs posterior packing (admit, monitor airway), endoscopic ligation or embolization.

name: Infraorbital artery
function: Branch of the third part of the maxillary artery that traverses the orbital floor with the infraorbital nerve and emerges on the face to supply the lower eyelid, cheek, nose and upper lip.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Third (pterygopalatine) part of the maxillary artery, often with the posterior superior alveolar artery.

details.label: Course
details.value: Enters the orbit through the inferior orbital fissure, runs in the infraorbital groove and canal in the orbital floor, and exits the infraorbital foramen deep to levator labii superioris.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Orbital branches (to inferior rectus/inferior oblique and the lacrimal sac), middle and anterior superior alveolar arteries (descend in the maxillary sinus wall to the premolar and anterior teeth), and terminal facial branches to the lower eyelid, nose and upper lip.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Lower eyelid, lacrimal sac, side of the nose, upper lip, cheek, maxillary sinus mucosa, upper premolars (middle superior alveolar) and incisors and canines (anterior superior alveolar).

details.label: Relations
details.value: Runs with the infraorbital nerve (V2); the infraorbital foramen lies about 1 cm below the orbital rim in line with the supraorbital and mental foramina.

pearl: Orbital floor (blowout) fractures involve the infraorbital canal, causing cheek and upper lip numbness (V2) with diplopia on upgaze from inferior rectus entrapment.

name: Superior and inferior labial arteries
function: Branches of the facial artery near the angle of the mouth that run within the lips and anastomose across the midline to form a continuous arterial ring around the oral fissure.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Facial artery just lateral to the angle of the mouth (inferior labial arises first).

details.label: Course
details.value: Run tortuously within the lip between the orbicularis oris and the mucous membrane, meeting the contralateral artery at the midline.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Superior labial: nasal septal branch to the anterior nasal septum (Kiesselbach plexus). Alar branches to the nose come from the lateral nasal branch of the facial artery, not from the superior labial. Both labial arteries give muscular and mucosal branches.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Upper and lower lips: orbicularis oris, levator labii superioris and levator anguli oris, zygomaticus major and minor, risorius (superior labial); depressor anguli oris, depressor labii inferioris, mentalis (inferior labial); labial glands and mucosa; nasalis, depressor septi and the anterior nasal septum (superior labial septal branch).

details.label: Relations
details.value: Lie deep to the vermilion between muscle and mucosa; palpable by pinching the lip.

pearl: Lip lacerations bleed from the labial artery just deep to the mucosa; pinch the lip to control. The septal branch of the superior labial artery feeds Kiesselbach plexus (anterior epistaxis).

name: Angular artery
function: Terminal part of the facial artery running from the side of the nose to the medial canthus, where it anastomoses with the dorsal nasal branch of the ophthalmic artery (ECA-ICA connection).

details.label: Origin
details.value: Continuation of the facial artery beyond the lateral nasal artery at the side of the nose.

details.label: Course
details.value: Ascends in the nasofacial groove to the medial angle of the eye, embedded in (deep to) the fibers of levator labii superioris alaeque nasi, having passed deep to zygomaticus major and the lip elevators.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Branches to the lacrimal sac, lower eyelid and root of the nose; anastomoses with dorsal nasal and palpebral branches of the ophthalmic artery.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Medial cheek, levator labii superioris and levator labii superioris alaeque nasi, procerus, lower eyelid, lacrimal sac and dorsum/root of the nose.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Accompanied by the angular vein (lateral to the artery), which drains to both the facial vein and, via the superior ophthalmic vein, the cavernous sinus (danger triangle of the face).

pearl: The angular-ophthalmic anastomosis gives retrograde collateral flow to the orbit in internal carotid occlusion and is the route by which filler injected near the nose can embolize to the retina and cause blindness.

name: Kiesselbach plexus (Little's area)
function: Anastomotic arterial plexus on the anteroinferior nasal septum where branches of the internal and external carotid systems meet; the site of most nosebleeds.

details.label: Location
details.value: Anteroinferior cartilaginous nasal septum, about 1 cm behind the mucocutaneous junction (vestibule).

details.label: Contributing arteries
details.value: Anterior ethmoidal (ophthalmic/ICA), sphenopalatine (maxillary), greater palatine (maxillary) and septal branch of the superior labial artery (facial).

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Anterior septal mucosa; thin, exposed mucosa over cartilage with little cushioning.

details.label: Why it bleeds
details.value: Exposed to drying air, digital trauma and inflammation; vessels lie superficially over cartilage with no overlying protection.

pearl: About 90% of epistaxis is anterior from Kiesselbach plexus (nose picking, dry air, rhinitis); treat with pinching the soft nose for 10-15 minutes, oxymetazoline, silver nitrate cautery or anterior packing.

name: Transverse facial artery
function: Branch of the superficial temporal artery that runs forward across the masseter parallel to and above the parotid duct, supplying the parotid, masseter and skin of the cheek.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Superficial temporal artery within the parotid gland, before it leaves the gland.

details.label: Course
details.value: Passes forward across the masseter between the zygomatic arch (above) and the parotid duct (below), accompanied by branches of the facial nerve.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Glandular branches to the parotid, muscular branches to masseter, and cutaneous branches to the cheek, anastomosing with the facial and infraorbital arteries.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Parotid gland and duct, masseter, TMJ, skin of the cheek.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Lies in the same plane as the buccal and zygomatic branches of CN VII; the parotid duct lies about 1 cm below it.

pearl: A laceration of the cheek along a line from the tragus to the upper lip can divide the transverse facial artery, parotid duct and buccal branches of the facial nerve together; check for duct injury and facial weakness.

name: Subclavian artery
function: Supplies the upper limb, brain (vertebral), neck, thoracic wall and spinal cord. Divided into three parts by the anterior scalene muscle.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Right: brachiocephalic trunk behind the right sternoclavicular joint. Left: directly from the aortic arch.

details.label: Course
details.value: Arches laterally over the pleura and first rib, posterior to the anterior scalene, and becomes the axillary artery at the outer border of the first rib.

details.label: Parts and branches
details.value: 1st part (medial to anterior scalene): vertebral, internal thoracic, thyrocervical trunk. 2nd part (behind anterior scalene): costocervical trunk. 3rd part (lateral): dorsal scapular (variable). Mnemonic VIT C D.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Upper limb, brainstem and posterior brain, thyroid, neck and shoulder muscles, anterior chest wall, cervical spinal cord.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Subclavian vein lies anterior to anterior scalene (artery behind it); phrenic nerve descends on anterior scalene; brachial plexus trunks lie posterolateral to the 3rd part; pleural dome and stellate ganglion lie below.

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Right subclavian (from the brachiocephalic trunk) and left subclavian (from the aortic arch). Each has three parts by its relation to the anterior scalene. 1st part (medial to the muscle): vertebral artery, internal thoracic artery, thyrocervical trunk. 2nd part (behind the muscle): costocervical trunk. 3rd part (lateral to the muscle, to the outer border of the 1st rib): dorsal scapular artery when it does not arise from the transverse cervical.

pearl: Subclavian steal: proximal subclavian stenosis reverses vertebral flow with arm exercise, giving arm claudication, vertebrobasilar symptoms (dizziness, syncope) and a >15 mmHg interarm BP difference. Subclavian line: arterial puncture is non-compressible behind the clavicle; pneumothorax is the other key complication.

name: Vertebral artery
function: First branch of the subclavian; ascends through the cervical transverse foramina to supply the brainstem, cerebellum, cervical spinal cord and posterior cerebrum via the basilar artery.

details.label: Origin
details.value: First part of the subclavian artery, medial to anterior scalene (first and largest branch).

details.label: Course
details.value: V1: ascends between longus colli and anterior scalene to enter the C6 transverse foramen. V2: through the C6-C1 transverse foramina. V3: winds behind the lateral mass of the atlas in the groove on the posterior arch of C1 and pierces the posterior atlanto-occipital membrane and dura. V4: through the foramen magnum, joins its fellow at the pontomedullary junction to form the basilar.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Cervical part: spinal (segmental medullary) and muscular branches to the prevertebral and suboccipital muscles. Intracranial part: anterior and posterior meningeal branches, posterior inferior cerebellar artery (PICA), posterior spinal artery (from the vertebral or from PICA) and anterior spinal artery, which unites with its fellow before the vertebrals form the basilar.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Medulla, cerebellum (PICA), cervical spinal cord (spinal and segmental medullary branches), prevertebral and suboccipital neck muscles (longus colli/capitis, recti capitis), and posterior fossa dura (meningeal branches); posterior circulation via the basilar.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Lies anterior to the cervical ventral rami within the foramina; the C7 transverse foramen is usually bypassed; accompanied by a vertebral venous plexus and sympathetic fibers.

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Prevertebral part (V1): subclavian to the transverse foramen of C6. Cervical part (V2): through the transverse foramina of C6 to C1; segmental medullary and muscular branches. Atlantic part (V3, horizontal segment): in the groove on the posterior arch of the atlas within the suboccipital triangle. Intracranial part (V4): through the foramen magnum; anterior and posterior meningeal branches, posterior spinal, posterior inferior cerebellar and anterior spinal arteries, then joins its fellow as the basilar.

pearl: Vertebral artery dissection (neck trauma, chiropractic manipulation): neck/occipital pain then lateral medullary (Wallenberg) syndrome or PICA stroke; diagnose with CTA/MRA, treat with antithrombotics.

name: Thyrocervical trunk
function: Short trunk from the first part of the subclavian at the medial border of anterior scalene; divides almost at once into the inferior thyroid, transverse cervical and suprascapular arteries.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Upper surface of the first part of the subclavian artery, medial to the anterior scalene, lateral to the vertebral artery.

details.label: Course
details.value: Ascends only a few millimetres before dividing.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Inferior thyroid artery (ascends), transverse cervical artery and suprascapular artery (both run laterally across anterior scalene and the phrenic nerve); ascending cervical usually arises from the inferior thyroid, sometimes separately.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Thyroid and parathyroids, larynx, trachea, esophagus and pharynx (inferior thyroid); scalene and prevertebral muscles (ascending cervical); SCM and platysma (suprascapular); trapezius, levator scapulae and rhomboids (transverse cervical); scapular region.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Phrenic nerve descends on anterior scalene deep to the transverse cervical and suprascapular arteries; the vagus and internal jugular vein lie anteromedially.

pearl: Scapular anastomosis: suprascapular and transverse cervical branches link to the subscapular artery, so flow to the arm continues if the axillary artery is occluded between the thyrocervical trunk and the subscapular artery. Its transverse branches cross the phrenic nerve on anterior scalene, a hazard in supraclavicular dissection.

name: Inferior thyroid artery
function: Largest branch of the thyrocervical trunk; the main supply of the lower thyroid, parathyroid glands, larynx below the cords, trachea and esophagus.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Thyrocervical trunk from the first part of the subclavian artery.

details.label: Course
details.value: Ascends along the medial border of anterior scalene in front of the vertebral artery and longus colli, then at C6 turns medially behind the carotid sheath and sympathetic trunk (middle cervical ganglion) to reach the posterior surface of the thyroid lobe.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Inferior laryngeal, tracheal, esophageal, pharyngeal, ascending cervical and glandular branches.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Lower thyroid lobe, both parathyroid glands (superior and inferior), larynx via the inferior laryngeal artery (the intrinsic laryngeal muscles, including cricothyroid, are shared with the superior thyroid artery), trachea, esophagus, pharynx; via the ascending cervical artery the scalenes, longus colli/capitis and other prevertebral muscles.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Recurrent laryngeal nerve crosses its terminal branches (anterior, posterior or between) near the gland; the middle cervical ganglion lies on the artery.

pearl: Thyroidectomy: the recurrent laryngeal nerve runs with the inferior thyroid artery; identify the nerve and ligate the artery's branches at the capsule, not the trunk, to keep the parathyroids perfused (hypocalcemia).

name: Transverse cervical artery
function: Branch of the thyrocervical trunk that crosses the posterior triangle to supply trapezius, levator scapulae and the rhomboids (via its deep branch, the dorsal scapular artery).

details.label: Origin
details.value: Thyrocervical trunk (its deep branch may arise directly from the third part of the subclavian as the dorsal scapular artery, which then passes through the brachial plexus trunks).

details.label: Course
details.value: Runs laterally and backward over the anterior scalene and phrenic nerve, crosses the posterior triangle in front of (occasionally between) the brachial plexus trunks, higher than the suprascapular artery, and divides at the anterior border of levator scapulae.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Superficial branch (runs deep to trapezius with the accessory nerve) and deep branch / dorsal scapular artery (deep to rhomboids along the medial scapular border).

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Trapezius (superficial branch, with CN XI), levator scapulae and rhomboids (deep branch/dorsal scapular), scalenus posterior (superficial branch), skin of the posterior triangle; part of the scapular anastomosis.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Passes anterior to the brachial plexus trunks and above the suprascapular artery; accessory nerve (CN XI) accompanies the superficial branch deep to trapezius.

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Superficial branch (superficial cervical artery): deep to trapezius with the accessory nerve. Deep branch (dorsal scapular artery): deep to levator scapulae and the rhomboids along the medial border of the scapula; arises with the superficial branch in about 30%, otherwise directly from the subclavian.

pearl: Accessory nerve and transverse cervical vessels run together under trapezius; cervical lymph node biopsy in the posterior triangle risks CN XI injury (shoulder droop, weak shrug).

name: Suprascapular artery
function: Branch of the thyrocervical trunk that runs laterally behind the clavicle to the scapular notch, supplying supraspinatus and infraspinatus and joining the scapular anastomosis.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Thyrocervical trunk (sometimes directly from the third part of the subclavian).

details.label: Course
details.value: Passes laterally across the anterior scalene and phrenic nerve, in front of the brachial plexus trunks, behind the clavicle to the superior transverse scapular ligament, over which it passes (the nerve passes beneath).

details.label: Branches
details.value: Suprasternal, acromial, articular (shoulder and AC joints) and muscular branches; anastomoses with the circumflex scapular and dorsal scapular arteries.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Supraspinatus and infraspinatus, shoulder and acromioclavicular joints, clavicle and scapula; in the neck, muscular branches to SCM and platysma.

details.label: Relations
details.value: 'Army over, Navy under': the artery passes over the superior transverse scapular ligament, the suprascapular nerve under it through the notch.

pearl: Suprascapular nerve entrapment: scapular notch (artery over ligament, spared) weakens abduction and external rotation; spinoglenoid notch (volleyball ganglion cyst) isolated infraspinatus wasting, weak external rotation.

name: Costocervical trunk
function: Branch of the second part of the subclavian that arches back over the pleural dome and divides into the deep cervical artery (posterior neck) and supreme intercostal artery (1st and 2nd intercostal spaces).

details.label: Origin
details.value: Posterior surface of the second part of the subclavian (behind anterior scalene) on the right; usually the first part on the left.

details.label: Course
details.value: Arches backward above the cervical pleura to the neck of the first rib, where it divides.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Deep cervical artery (ascends between semispinalis capitis and cervicis, anastomoses with the descending branch of the occipital artery); supreme (superior) intercostal artery (gives the posterior intercostal arteries of spaces 1 and 2).

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Deep posterior neck muscles, upper two intercostal spaces, spinal branches to the cervical cord.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Lies just above the pleural dome and stellate ganglion, a hazard in supraclavicular and first-rib approaches.

pearl: In aortic coarctation, rib notching spares ribs 1-2 because their posterior intercostals come from the supreme intercostal (subclavian), not the aorta; the deep cervical artery also collateralizes the vertebral system in proximal subclavian occlusion.

name: Internal thoracic artery (origin)
function: Arises from the inferior surface of the first part of the subclavian and descends behind the clavicle and costal cartilages to supply the anterior chest wall, breast, pericardium and diaphragm.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Inferior surface of the first part of the subclavian, opposite the thyrocervical trunk, medial to anterior scalene.

details.label: Course
details.value: Descends behind the clavicle and subclavian vein, crossed by the phrenic nerve, and runs about 1 cm lateral to the sternal border behind the costal cartilages to the 6th space, dividing into musculophrenic and superior epigastric arteries.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Pericardiacophrenic (with phrenic nerve), anterior intercostals, perforating (to breast), mediastinal, musculophrenic, superior epigastric.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Anterior chest wall, medial breast, pericardium, diaphragm, anterior abdominal wall (via superior epigastric).

details.label: Relations
details.value: Phrenic nerve crosses it from lateral to medial at the thoracic inlet; subclavian vein lies in front at its origin.

pearl: Left internal thoracic (mammary) artery is the preferred CABG conduit to the LAD. In aortic coarctation it enlarges as a collateral; the dilated posterior intercostals it feeds notch the inferior rib margins on CXR.

name: Thyroid ima artery (variant)
function: Inconstant (about 3-10%) artery that ascends on the anterior trachea to the thyroid isthmus; a bleeding hazard in tracheostomy and thyroid surgery.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Variable: brachiocephalic trunk most commonly, or the aortic arch, right common carotid, subclavian or internal thoracic artery.

details.label: Course
details.value: Ascends in the midline in front of the trachea, within the pretracheal space, to the lower border of the thyroid isthmus.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Tracheal and glandular branches.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Thyroid isthmus and lower poles, upper trachea; may be the dominant supply when inferior thyroid arteries are absent.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Lies directly in the path of a midline tracheostomy below the isthmus, together with the inferior thyroid veins; it is not encountered in cricothyroidotomy, which is above the isthmus through the cricothyroid membrane.

pearl: Thyroid ima artery and inferior thyroid veins lie in front of the trachea below the isthmus; they cause brisk bleeding during low tracheostomy, so dissection stays in the midline with careful hemostasis. Cricothyroidotomy (above the isthmus) avoids them.

name: Ophthalmic artery
function: First intracranial branch of the internal carotid; enters the orbit through the optic canal to supply the eye, orbit, forehead, lacrimal gland and anterior nasal cavity.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Internal carotid artery as it leaves the cavernous sinus, medial to the anterior clinoid process.

details.label: Course
details.value: Passes through the optic canal below and lateral to the optic nerve (inside the dural sheath), crosses above the nerve to the medial orbital wall, and ends as the supratrochlear and dorsal nasal arteries.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Central retinal, lacrimal, long and short posterior ciliary, muscular, supraorbital, posterior and anterior ethmoidal, medial palpebral, supratrochlear, dorsal nasal.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Retina (central retinal), choroid, iris and ciliary body including the ciliary, sphincter and dilator pupillae muscles (posterior and anterior ciliary), all extraocular muscles and levator palpebrae superioris (muscular branches), lacrimal gland, eyelids, forehead and scalp, ethmoid cells, frontal sinus and anterior nasal cavity (ethmoidal), and dura of the anterior fossa (anterior meningeal).

details.label: Relations
details.value: Runs with the optic nerve; anastomoses with the external carotid via the angular, facial and middle meningeal arteries.

pearl: Amaurosis fugax (transient monocular 'curtain' blindness) is an embolus from carotid plaque into the ophthalmic/retinal circulation; it is a TIA equivalent and warrants carotid duplex and risk-factor control.

name: Central retinal artery
function: Small end artery from the ophthalmic that pierces the optic nerve and supplies the inner retina; occlusion causes sudden painless monocular blindness.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Ophthalmic artery, usually its first branch, within the orbit near the optic canal.

details.label: Course
details.value: Runs forward beneath the optic nerve, pierces its dural sheath about 1 cm behind the globe, travels in the center of the nerve and emerges at the optic disc, dividing into superior and inferior (nasal/temporal) retinal arterioles.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Four retinal arteriolar branches; a true end artery with no anastomoses. A cilioretinal artery (from the posterior ciliary circulation) in about 20% of people can spare the macula in CRAO.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Inner two-thirds of the retina (ganglion cell and bipolar layers); the outer retina and foveal photoreceptors are supplied by the choroid (posterior ciliary arteries).

details.label: Relations
details.value: Accompanied by the central retinal vein within the optic nerve; raised intracranial pressure compresses the vein, producing papilledema.

pearl: Central retinal artery occlusion: sudden painless monocular vision loss with RAPD, pale retina and cherry-red macula (choroid showing through the fovea); embolic from carotid or cardiac source, or giant cell arteritis (check ESR/CRP in patients over 50).

name: Anterior ethmoidal artery
function: Branch of the ophthalmic artery that leaves the orbit through the anterior ethmoidal foramen to supply the anterior ethmoid cells, frontal sinus, anterior fossa dura and the anterosuperior nasal cavity.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Ophthalmic artery on the medial orbital wall, larger than the posterior ethmoidal artery.

details.label: Course
details.value: Passes through the anterior ethmoidal foramen (fronto-ethmoid suture) with the anterior ethmoidal nerve into the anterior cranial fossa, then descends through the cribriform plate into the nasal cavity, ending as the external nasal artery on the dorsum.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Anterior meningeal branch, branches to anterior/middle ethmoid cells and frontal sinus, lateral and septal nasal branches, external nasal branch.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Anterior ethmoid and frontal sinuses, anterior fossa dura, anterosuperior nasal septum and lateral wall (contributes to Kiesselbach plexus), skin of the nasal dorsum.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Crosses the ethmoid roof in a thin bony canal just behind the frontal recess, at the skull base. Its nasal branches are the internal carotid's contribution to the nasal supply; posterior epistaxis is usually sphenopalatine (external carotid).

pearl: Anterior ethmoidal artery is the usual culprit in epistaxis after naso-orbito-ethmoid or anterior skull base fracture; if cut it can retract into the orbit and cause an orbital hematoma (proptosis, vision loss), and it is a key skull-base landmark in endoscopic sinus surgery.

name: Supraorbital and supratrochlear arteries
function: Terminal forehead branches of the ophthalmic artery (internal carotid system) that exit the orbit at the supraorbital margin and supply the forehead and anterior scalp.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Ophthalmic artery: supraorbital arises as it crosses the optic nerve; supratrochlear is one of its two terminal branches.

details.label: Course
details.value: Supraorbital leaves through the supraorbital notch/foramen with the supraorbital nerve (V1); supratrochlear exits at the medial orbital margin above the trochlea with the supratrochlear nerve. Both ascend the forehead deep to frontalis.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Superficial and deep branches to skin, frontalis, pericranium and frontal bone (diploic branches).

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Forehead, upper eyelid, anterior scalp to the vertex; anastomose with the frontal branch of the superficial temporal artery (ECA).

details.label: Relations
details.value: Supraorbital foramen lies on a vertical line with the infraorbital and mental foramina, about 2.5 cm from the midline; the paramedian forehead flap is based on the supratrochlear artery.

pearl: Scalp lacerations bleed profusely because scalp arteries are tethered in dense connective tissue and cannot retract; forehead anesthesia uses supraorbital/supratrochlear nerve block at the orbital rim.

name: Basilar artery
function: Formed by the union of the two vertebral arteries at the pontomedullary junction; supplies the pons, cerebellum, inner ear and, via the posterior cerebral arteries, the occipital and medial temporal lobes.

details.label: Formation
details.value: Union of the right and left vertebral arteries at the lower border of the pons (pontomedullary junction).

details.label: Course
details.value: Ascends in the midline basilar sulcus of the pons on the clivus, within the pontine cistern, and divides at the upper border of the pons into the two posterior cerebral arteries.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Anterior inferior cerebellar (AICA), labyrinthine (often from AICA), pontine (paramedian and circumferential), superior cerebellar, posterior cerebral (terminal).

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Pons, midbrain, cerebellum, inner ear, thalamus and the posterior cerebral territory.

details.label: Relations
details.value: CN VI emerges at the pontomedullary junction (medial to CN VII/VIII), lateral to the basilar artery, and ascends in the prepontine cistern between the pons and the clivus, closely related to AICA; CN III passes between the posterior cerebral and superior cerebellar arteries (compressed by PCom aneurysms).

pearl: Basilar occlusion causes locked-in syndrome (ventral pons: quadriplegia, anarthria, preserved consciousness and vertical gaze); 'top of the basilar' gives cortical blindness and midbrain signs. Treat with thrombectomy.

name: Circle of Willis
function: Arterial anastomotic ring at the base of the brain around the optic chiasm and pituitary stalk that links the internal carotid (anterior) and vertebrobasilar (posterior) circulations.

details.label: Components
details.value: Anterior communicating artery, two anterior cerebral arteries (A1), two internal carotids, two posterior communicating arteries, two posterior cerebral arteries (P1) joined by the basilar bifurcation.

details.label: Location
details.value: Interpeduncular cistern on the base of the brain, surrounding the optic chiasm, infundibulum and mammillary bodies, above the sella turcica.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Anterior cerebral (medial frontal/parietal, leg area; gives the recurrent artery of Heubner and anteromedial central perforators), middle cerebral (lateral hemisphere, face/arm area, Broca and Wernicke; anterolateral central/lenticulostriate perforators), posterior cerebral (occipital, medial temporal; thalamoperforating and posteromedial central perforators, posterior choroidal arteries), anterior choroidal, and superior/inferior hypophyseal and hypothalamic branches.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Entire cerebrum; the ring allows collateral flow if one feeding vessel is occluded, though it is complete in only about one-third of people.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Optic chiasm lies within the circle; CN III passes close to the posterior communicating artery; pituitary stalk in the center.

pearl: Saccular (berry) aneurysms arise at circle branch points, most often the anterior communicating artery (visual field/frontal signs) and PCom (painful CN III palsy with dilated pupil); rupture gives thunderclap-headache subarachnoid hemorrhage.

name: Posterior communicating artery
function: Links the internal carotid (anterior circulation) to the posterior cerebral artery (posterior circulation), forming the lateral limb of the circle of Willis; gives perforators to the thalamus and hypothalamus.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Posterior wall of the supraclinoid (communicating) segment of the internal carotid artery, after the ophthalmic artery and before the anterior choroidal artery and the ICA terminal bifurcation.

details.label: Course
details.value: Runs posteriorly above and medial to the oculomotor nerve (CN III), medial to the uncus and lateral to the pituitary stalk and mammillary bodies, through the interpeduncular cistern to join the P1-P2 junction of the PCA.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Posteromedial central (perforating) arteries to the hypothalamus, optic tract and anterior/medial thalamus, including the thalamotuberal (premammillary) artery; the thalamoperforating arteries proper arise from the P1 segment of the posterior cerebral artery.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Collateral between anterior and posterior circulations; perforators to anterior/medial thalamus and hypothalamus. A 'fetal PComm' (large PComm with hypoplastic P1, ~20%) means the PCA territory depends on the carotid.

details.label: Relations
details.value: CN III passes immediately inferolateral to it, emerging between the PCA and superior cerebellar artery; a PComm aneurysm (usually pointing posterolaterally) sits directly on the nerve.

pearl: PComm aneurysm compresses CN III: painful ipsilateral ptosis, 'down-and-out' eye and a dilated, fixed pupil. Pupil involvement (superficial parasympathetic fibers) distinguishes compression from pupil-sparing diabetic/ischemic CN III palsy; obtain urgent CTA/MRA.

name: Anterior communicating artery
function: Short midline vessel joining the two anterior cerebral arteries above the optic chiasm; completes the anterior limb of the circle of Willis and equalizes flow between the two carotid systems.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Connects the A1 segments of the right and left anterior cerebral arteries at the junction with their A2 segments, in the midline within the lamina terminalis cistern.

details.label: Course
details.value: Very short (about 2-3 mm), runs transversely across the midline immediately superior to the optic chiasm (or optic nerves) and anterior to the lamina terminalis; often fenestrated or duplicated.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Anteromedial central (perforating) arteries to the optic chiasm, lamina terminalis, anterior hypothalamus, columns of the fornix, septum pellucidum and genu/rostrum of the corpus callosum (subcallosal/median callosal branches).

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Collateral between the two anterior circulations; perforators to the hypothalamus, fornix and septal region, so injury causes memory loss (anterograde amnesia) and personality change.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Lies directly above the optic chiasm/optic nerves and below the gyrus rectus; an aneurysm here projects toward the chiasm or into the frontal lobe.

pearl: Most common site of saccular (berry) aneurysm and aneurysmal SAH ('worst headache of my life'). Can compress the optic chiasm (bitemporal hemianopia); rupture may cause frontal hematoma and amnesia/confabulation.

name: Tonsillar branch of the facial artery
function: The principal arterial supply of the palatine tonsil; arises from the cervical part of the facial artery and pierces the superior pharyngeal constrictor to reach the lower pole of the tonsil.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Cervical part of the facial artery near its origin, close to the ascending palatine artery, as it ascends deep to the posterior belly of digastric/stylohyoid toward the submandibular gland (sometimes from the ascending palatine).

details.label: Course
details.value: Ascends between the medial pterygoid and the styloglossus, pierces the superior pharyngeal constrictor and enters the lower pole of the palatine tonsil through the tonsillar bed.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Terminal twigs within the tonsil; small branches to the root of the tongue and the adjacent pharyngeal wall.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Palatine tonsil (main supply) and the lower tonsillar bed; with the ascending palatine, the superior and middle pharyngeal constrictors and stylopharyngeus. Minor tonsillar contributors: ascending palatine, ascending pharyngeal, dorsal lingual and lesser palatine (from descending palatine) arteries.

details.label: Relations
details.value: The internal carotid artery lies about 2-2.5 cm posterolateral to the tonsillar fossa, deep to the superior constrictor, so deep lateral dissection in the tonsillar bed is hazardous.

pearl: Post-tonsillectomy bleed (primary <24 h; secondary ~5-10 d as eschar sloughs) is usually from the tonsillar artery/bed; brisk bleeding needs OR. Drain peritonsillar abscess shallow (<1 cm) and never laterally (ICA).

name: Greater palatine artery
function: Terminal branch of the descending palatine artery (third part of the maxillary) that exits the greater palatine foramen and runs forward to supply the hard palate mucosa, palatal gingiva and glands.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Descending palatine artery, a branch of the pterygopalatine (third) part of the maxillary artery in the pterygopalatine fossa; the smaller lesser palatine branches go to the soft palate and tonsil.

details.label: Course
details.value: Descends in the greater palatine canal with the greater palatine nerve, emerges at the greater palatine foramen (medial to the 2nd/3rd maxillary molar) and runs anteriorly in a groove along the hard palate to the incisive canal.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Branches to the palatal gingiva, palatine glands and mucosa; terminal branch ascends through the incisive canal to anastomose with the sphenopalatine (posterior septal) branches on the nasal septum.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Hard palate mucosa, palatal gingiva, periosteum and palatine glands; via the lesser palatine arteries the soft palate muscles (levator and tensor veli palatini, musculus uvulae, palatopharyngeus, palatoglossus) and tonsil; contributes to Kiesselbach plexus on the anterior nasal septum via the incisive canal.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Lies in the groove between the palate and alveolar process; palatal flap and dental surgery, and harvesting of connective-tissue grafts, must avoid the foramen region.

pearl: Part of Kiesselbach plexus (with anterior ethmoidal, sphenopalatine, superior labial): anterior epistaxis. Surgery or injection at the greater palatine foramen risks brisk bleeding or ischemic palatal necrosis.

name: Anterior cerebral artery (A1, A2, pericallosal, callosomarginal)
function: Smaller terminal branch of the internal carotid that runs medially above the optic nerve, joins its partner through the anterior communicating artery and then curls over the corpus callosum to supply the medial surface of the frontal and parietal lobes.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Terminal division of the internal carotid artery lateral to the optic chiasm.

details.label: Course
details.value: A1 segment runs medially above the optic nerve to the anterior communicating artery; A2 segment ascends in the longitudinal fissure in front of the lamina terminalis and continues over the genu and body of the corpus callosum as the pericallosal artery.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Anteromedial central (perforating) arteries and the long medial striate artery (recurrent artery of Heubner) from A1–proximal A2; medial frontobasal (orbitofrontal), frontopolar, callosomarginal (anterior, intermediate and posterior medial frontal branches, paracentral), pericallosal and precuneal branches.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Medial surface of the frontal and parietal lobes to the parieto-occipital sulcus, the paracentral lobule (leg and foot area of the motor and sensory cortex), the anterior corpus callosum, and via Heubner's artery the head of the caudate, anterior limb of the internal capsule and anterior putamen.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Crosses the optic nerve and chiasm; the anterior communicating artery joins the two A1 segments above the chiasm.

details.label: Divisions
details.value: A1 (precommunicating) segment: internal carotid to anterior communicating artery; anteromedial central arteries. A2 (postcommunicating) segment: in the longitudinal fissure; long medial striate artery (recurrent artery of Heubner), medial frontobasal (orbitofrontal) artery, frontopolar artery. Terminal trunks: callosomarginal artery (anterior, intermediate and posterior medial frontal branches, cingular branches, paracentral artery) and pericallosal artery (precuneal artery, terminal branches to the medial parietal lobe).

pearl: ACA stroke: contralateral leg-predominant weakness and sensory loss with urinary incontinence, abulia and sometimes a grasp reflex; bilateral ACA infarction after AComm aneurysm rupture or vasospasm causes akinetic mutism. Heubner's artery occlusion gives face and arm weakness from the internal capsule.

name: Middle cerebral artery (M1–M4, lenticulostriate and cortical branches)
function: Larger terminal branch of the internal carotid that runs laterally in the sylvian fissure and supplies most of the lateral hemisphere, the insula and the deep gray matter; the artery most often occluded in ischemic stroke.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Direct continuation of the internal carotid artery lateral to the optic chiasm.

details.label: Course
details.value: M1 (sphenoidal) segment runs laterally below the anterior perforated substance to the limen insulae; M2 (insular) branches fan over the insula; M3 (opercular) branches run under the frontal, parietal and temporal opercula; M4 cortical branches emerge from the lateral sulcus onto the convexity.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Anterolateral central (lenticulostriate) arteries from M1; lateral frontobasal (orbitofrontal), prefrontal, arteries of the precentral, central and postcentral sulcus (anterior parietal), posterior parietal, artery to the angular gyrus, and anterior, middle and posterior temporal branches.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Lateral frontal, parietal and temporal cortex including the face and arm areas of the motor and sensory strips, Broca and Wernicke areas (left), the insula and auditory cortex; lenticulostriate branches supply the putamen, globus pallidus, caudate body and the genu and posterior limb of the internal capsule.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Lies in the lateral (sylvian) sulcus deep to the temporalis and pterion; the superficial middle cerebral vein accompanies it.

details.label: Divisions
details.value: M1 (sphenoidal) segment: anterolateral central (lenticulostriate) arteries. M2 (insular) segment: superior and inferior trunks over the insula. M3 (opercular) and M4 (cortical) segments, giving in order: lateral frontobasal (orbitofrontal) artery, prefrontal artery, artery of precentral sulcus, artery of central sulcus, artery of postcentral sulcus (anterior parietal), posterior parietal artery, artery to angular gyrus, and anterior, middle and posterior temporal branches (with the polar temporal artery).

pearl: MCA stroke: contralateral face and arm weakness and sensory loss, gaze deviation toward the lesion, homonymous hemianopia, aphasia if dominant (Broca: superior division; Wernicke: inferior division) or neglect if non-dominant. Lenticulostriate occlusion from hypertension causes lacunar pure motor stroke or Charcot–Bouchard microaneurysm bleeds into the putamen. M1 occlusion is the classic thrombectomy target (dense MCA sign).

name: Posterior cerebral artery (P1, P2, calcarine, parieto-occipital, choroidal branches)
function: Terminal branch of the basilar artery that winds around the midbrain to supply the occipital lobe, the inferomedial temporal lobe, the thalamus and the midbrain; connected to the internal carotid by the posterior communicating artery.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Terminal division of the basilar artery at the upper border of the pons; embryologically a carotid branch, so a fetal-type PCA from the internal carotid is a common variant.

details.label: Course
details.value: P1 segment runs laterally from the basilar bifurcation to the junction with the posterior communicating artery; P2 segment curves around the cerebral crus above the tentorium and the oculomotor nerve; P3/P4 continue on the inferior surface of the temporal and occipital lobes to the calcarine sulcus.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Thalamoperforating (posteromedial central) arteries from P1; thalamogeniculate arteries and posterior medial and lateral choroidal arteries from P2; anterior and posterior temporal (occipitotemporal) branches; parieto-occipital and calcarine branches; dorsal branch to the corpus callosum (posterior pericallosal).

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Occipital lobe including the primary visual cortex (calcarine), the medial and inferior temporal lobe including the hippocampus and parahippocampal gyrus, the thalamus, subthalamus and cerebral peduncle of the midbrain, the choroid plexus of the 3rd and lateral ventricles and the splenium.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Oculomotor nerve passes between the posterior cerebral and superior cerebellar arteries; the posterior communicating artery joins P1 to the internal carotid; the basal vein accompanies P2 around the midbrain.

details.label: Divisions
details.value: P1 (precommunicating) segment: basilar bifurcation to the posterior communicating artery; thalamoperforating (posteromedial central) arteries. P2 (postcommunicating) segment: around the cerebral crus; thalamogeniculate arteries, posterior medial and posterior lateral choroidal arteries. Cortical branches: anterior and posterior temporal and occipitotemporal branches (lateral occipital artery), and the medial occipital artery giving the dorsal branch to corpus callosum (posterior pericallosal), parieto-occipital branch and calcarine branch.

pearl: PCA stroke: contralateral homonymous hemianopia with macular sparing (the occipital pole gets MCA collaterals), alexia without agraphia on the left, prosopagnosia and memory loss from hippocampal involvement; thalamic branches give contralateral sensory loss and thalamic pain. 'Top of the basilar' occlusion causes bilateral PCA infarcts with cortical blindness (Anton syndrome). Uncal herniation compresses the PCA against the tentorium, giving an occipital infarct.

name: Posterior inferior cerebellar artery (PICA)
function: Largest branch of the vertebral artery; winds around the medulla to supply its posterolateral part, the inferior cerebellar surface, the tonsil and the choroid plexus of the 4th ventricle.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Intracranial (V4) part of the vertebral artery below the vertebrobasilar junction.

details.label: Course
details.value: Passes backward around the lateral medulla between the rootlets of CN IX–XI, loops over the cerebellar tonsil (caudal loop) and runs up the inferior vermis and hemisphere.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Medullary branches to the lateral medulla, choroidal branch to the 4th ventricle, cerebellar tonsillar branch, inferior vermian artery and lateral hemispheric branches.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Lateral (dorsolateral) medulla: spinal trigeminal nucleus and tract, nucleus ambiguus, vestibular nuclei, spinothalamic tract, descending sympathetic fibers, inferior cerebellar peduncle; inferior surface of the cerebellum, tonsil and inferior vermis; choroid plexus of the 4th ventricle.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Accompanied by CN IX, X and XI as they leave the medulla; the posterior spinal artery often arises from it.

pearl: Lateral medullary (Wallenberg) syndrome from PICA or vertebral occlusion: ipsilateral facial pain and temperature loss, contralateral body pain and temperature loss, dysphagia and hoarseness (nucleus ambiguus), vertigo, nystagmus, ipsilateral Horner syndrome and ataxia, with no weakness. Vertebral dissection after neck manipulation is a classic cause in young adults. Cerebellar PICA infarcts swell and can compress the 4th ventricle (hydrocephalus) and tonsils.

name: Anterior inferior cerebellar artery (AICA)
function: Branch of the lower basilar artery that runs laterally across the pons toward the cerebellopontine angle and internal acoustic meatus, supplying the lateral pons, the middle cerebellar peduncle, the anteroinferior cerebellum and usually the inner ear via the labyrinthine artery.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Lower third of the basilar artery just above the vertebrobasilar junction.

details.label: Course
details.value: Runs posterolaterally around the pons in the cerebellopontine angle, looping near or into the internal acoustic meatus between CN VII and VIII, then onto the anteroinferior (petrosal) surface of the cerebellum.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Labyrinthine (internal acoustic) artery in most people, pontine branches, branches to the middle cerebellar peduncle, flocculus and anteroinferior hemisphere; anastomoses with PICA and the superior cerebellar artery.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Lateral caudal pons (facial nucleus and nerve, vestibular and cochlear nuclei, spinal trigeminal nucleus, spinothalamic tract), middle cerebellar peduncle, flocculus and anterior inferior cerebellum, and the inner ear through the labyrinthine artery.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Closely related to the facial and vestibulocochlear nerves at the cerebellopontine angle; CN VI emerges medial to it at the pontomedullary junction.

pearl: Lateral pontine (AICA) syndrome: ipsilateral facial paralysis (facial nucleus), ipsilateral deafness and vertigo (cochlear and vestibular nuclei or labyrinthine artery), ipsilateral facial sensory loss and ataxia, contralateral body pain and temperature loss and ipsilateral Horner syndrome. 'Facial droop means AICA's pooped.' Sudden unilateral sensorineural deafness with vertigo in a vascular patient is an AICA territory event.

name: Superior cerebellar artery
function: Last branch of the basilar artery before its bifurcation; runs below the oculomotor nerve around the midbrain to supply the superior cerebellum, the superior cerebellar peduncle and the upper pons.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Basilar artery just below the posterior cerebral arteries, at the upper border of the pons.

details.label: Course
details.value: Passes laterally around the cerebral peduncle below the tentorium and the oculomotor and trochlear nerves, then onto the superior (tentorial) surface of the cerebellum.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Lateral (marginal) branch to the hemisphere, superior vermian branch, branches to the superior cerebellar peduncle, dentate nucleus, upper pons and inferior colliculus.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Superior cerebellar hemisphere and vermis, dentate nucleus, superior and middle cerebellar peduncles, dorsolateral upper pons and lower midbrain including the spinothalamic tract and the inferior colliculus.

details.label: Relations
details.value: CN III emerges between the superior cerebellar and posterior cerebral arteries; CN IV runs below it around the midbrain; the trigeminal root lies lateral and below.

pearl: Superior cerebellar artery territory stroke: ipsilateral limb ataxia, intention tremor and dysarthria with contralateral pain and temperature loss, usually without the vertigo and deafness of the AICA syndrome. An aberrant loop of the SCA compressing the trigeminal root entry zone is the usual cause of classic trigeminal neuralgia, treated by microvascular decompression; a PCA/SCA aneurysm can compress CN III.

name: Labyrinthine (internal acoustic) artery
function: Long slender artery that enters the internal acoustic meatus with the facial and vestibulocochlear nerves and is the only arterial supply of the membranous labyrinth, so its occlusion silences the inner ear.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Usually the anterior inferior cerebellar artery, sometimes directly from the basilar artery.

details.label: Course
details.value: Runs laterally in the cerebellopontine angle with CN VII and CN VIII through the internal acoustic meatus into the petrous temporal bone.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Anterior vestibular, common cochlear and vestibulocochlear branches ending in the cochlea and vestibular labyrinth.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Cochlea (spiral organ via the modiolus), vestibule, semicircular ducts and the nerves in the meatus; the bony labyrinth itself receives twigs from the stylomastoid and tympanic arteries.

details.label: Relations
details.value: End artery with no collateral from the external carotid for the membranous labyrinth; accompanied by the labyrinthine veins to the inferior petrosal sinus.

pearl: An end artery: thrombosis or embolism causes sudden unilateral sensorineural hearing loss with vertigo ('labyrinthine infarction'), one of the vascular causes to consider in an older patient with sudden deafness. Compression in the internal acoustic meatus by a vestibular schwannoma contributes to the progressive hearing loss of acoustic neuroma.

name: Anterior choroidal artery
function: Small but critical branch of the internal carotid that runs backward along the optic tract to the temporal horn, supplying the posterior limb of the internal capsule, the optic tract and lateral geniculate body, the hippocampus and the choroid plexus of the lateral ventricle.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Supraclinoid internal carotid artery distal to the posterior communicating artery, just before the terminal bifurcation.

details.label: Course
details.value: Runs posterolaterally along the optic tract and around the cerebral peduncle, between the uncus and the crus cerebri, to enter the choroidal fissure of the temporal horn.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Perforators to the posterior limb and retrolenticular part of the internal capsule, globus pallidus, optic tract, lateral geniculate body, cerebral peduncle, uncus and hippocampus; terminal choroidal branches to the choroid plexus of the lateral ventricle (anastomosing with the posterior lateral choroidal artery).

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Posterior limb of the internal capsule (corticospinal and thalamocortical fibers), optic tract and lateral geniculate body (visual pathway), medial temporal lobe and hippocampus, medial globus pallidus, cerebral peduncle, choroid plexus.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Optic tract above and medial; uncus lateral; posterior communicating artery arises just proximal to it.

pearl: Anterior choroidal artery infarction gives the triad of contralateral hemiplegia (posterior limb of internal capsule), hemisensory loss and homonymous hemianopia (optic tract/lateral geniculate), often with sparing of language and cognition. It is vulnerable during aneurysm clipping of the internal carotid and in uncal herniation.

name: Anterior and posterior spinal arteries
function: Longitudinal arteries of the spinal cord that begin as branches of the vertebral arteries in the posterior cranial fossa: the single anterior spinal artery in the anterior median fissure supplies the anterior two-thirds of the cord and the medial medulla, the paired posterior spinal arteries supply the posterior columns.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Anterior spinal artery: a branch from each vertebral artery near the vertebrobasilar junction, the two uniting in the midline on the medulla. Posterior spinal arteries: from the vertebral artery or the posterior inferior cerebellar artery of each side.

details.label: Course
details.value: Anterior spinal artery descends through the foramen magnum in the anterior median fissure of the medulla and cord; posterior spinal arteries descend on the posterolateral cord beside the dorsal root entry zones. Both are reinforced along the cord by segmental (radicular) arteries, the largest being the artery of Adamkiewicz.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Sulcal (central) branches of the anterior spinal artery into the anterior median fissure; pial (vasocorona) anastomoses between anterior and posterior systems; medullary branches to the pyramids, medial lemniscus and hypoglossal nucleus.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Anterior spinal: medial medulla (pyramid, medial lemniscus, hypoglossal nerve and nucleus) and the anterior two-thirds of the cord (anterior horns, corticospinal and spinothalamic tracts). Posterior spinal: posterior columns and posterior horns.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Vertebral arteries and the medulla pass through the foramen magnum together; the anterior spinal artery lies in front of the pyramids.
