pearl: Medial medullary syndrome (anterior spinal artery): contralateral hemiparesis and loss of proprioception/vibration with ipsilateral tongue deviation. Anterior spinal artery syndrome of the cord (aortic surgery, dissection, hypotension): bilateral flaccid then spastic paralysis and loss of pain and temperature below the lesion with preserved vibration and proprioception, because the posterior spinal arteries are spared.

name: Petrous and cavernous branches of the internal carotid (caroticotympanic, meningohypophyseal and inferolateral trunks)
function: Small branches the internal carotid gives inside the temporal bone and cavernous sinus, before the ophthalmic artery; they supply the middle ear, the dura of the clivus and tentorium, the posterior pituitary and the cavernous sinus nerves, and form the internal-to-external carotid anastomoses used by collateral flow and by tumors.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Petrous part: caroticotympanic artery and the vidian (pterygoid canal) branch. Cavernous part: meningohypophyseal trunk, artery to the inferior cavernous sinus (inferolateral trunk) and small branches to the foramina rotundum, ovale and spinosum and the superior orbital fissure; a recurrent artery of the foramen lacerum.

details.label: Course
details.value: The caroticotympanic artery passes through the carotid canal wall into the tympanic cavity; the meningohypophyseal trunk arises from the posterior bend of the cavernous carotid; the inferolateral trunk crosses the abducens nerve laterally.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Meningohypophyseal trunk: tentorial (Bernasconi–Cassinari) artery, dorsal meningeal artery to the clivus and abducens nerve, inferior hypophyseal artery. Inferolateral trunk: branches to CN III, IV, VI and the gasserian ganglion, anastomosing through the foramina with the middle and accessory meningeal and ophthalmic arteries.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Middle ear mucosa (with the tympanic arteries), dura of the clivus, tentorium and cavernous sinus walls, posterior lobe of the pituitary, cavernous sinus cranial nerves and the trigeminal ganglion.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Within the cavernous sinus the carotid is accompanied by CN VI and sympathetic fibers; these branches anastomose with the external carotid system through the foramen lacerum, rotundum, ovale and spinosum.

pearl: These are the feeders of cavernous sinus dural arteriovenous fistulas and of tentorial meningiomas (enlarged tentorial artery on angiography), and the routes by which the external carotid supplies the brain when the proximal internal carotid is occluded. A cavernous carotid aneurysm compresses CN VI and III rather than bleeding into the subarachnoid space.

name: Superior and inferior hypophyseal arteries
function: Pituitary arteries: the superior hypophyseal arteries from the supraclinoid internal carotid feed the hypothalamic median eminence and stalk and so the portal system of the anterior lobe, while the inferior hypophyseal arteries from the cavernous carotid supply the posterior lobe directly.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Superior hypophyseal arteries: supraclinoid (cerebral) part of the internal carotid and posterior communicating artery, medial to the optic nerve. Inferior hypophyseal artery: meningohypophyseal trunk of the cavernous internal carotid.

details.label: Course
details.value: Superior branches run medially below the optic chiasm to the infundibulum and tuber cinereum; inferior branches pass medially through the cavernous sinus to the posterior lobe and capsule.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Superior: capillary plexus of the median eminence and upper stalk that drains into the long hypophyseal portal veins; branches to the optic chiasm and optic nerve. Inferior: capillary plexus of the neurohypophysis and lower stalk, short portal veins, capsular branches.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Anterior lobe indirectly through the hypophyseal portal veins (carrying hypothalamic releasing hormones), the stalk, optic chiasm and optic nerves; posterior lobe directly.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Optic chiasm immediately above the superior arteries; cavernous sinus and the efferent hypophyseal veins around the gland.

pearl: The anterior pituitary has no direct arterial supply of its own, which makes it vulnerable: postpartum hypotension infarcts the hyperplastic gland (Sheehan syndrome: failure of lactation, amenorrhea, hypothyroidism, adrenal insufficiency), and pituitary apoplexy is hemorrhagic infarction of an adenoma with sudden headache, visual loss and adrenal crisis. The posterior lobe, supplied directly, is usually spared in Sheehan syndrome.

name: Brachiocephalic trunk
function: First and largest branch of the aortic arch; ascends to the right behind the manubrium and divides behind the right sternoclavicular joint into the right common carotid and right subclavian arteries. There is no left brachiocephalic artery.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Aortic arch, behind the manubrium.

details.label: Course
details.value: Runs upward and to the right in front of the trachea and behind the left brachiocephalic vein and the sternohyoid and sternothyroid muscles to the upper border of the right sternoclavicular joint.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Right common carotid artery and right subclavian artery; occasionally a thyroid ima artery to the thyroid isthmus.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Right side of the head and neck and the right upper limb through its two terminal branches.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Trachea posterior and left, left brachiocephalic vein crossing in front, right brachiocephalic vein and vagus lateral, thymus in front in children.

pearl: A tracheostomy placed too low, or a cuffed tube eroding the anterior tracheal wall, can create a tracheo-innominate fistula with massive hemoptysis (overinflate the cuff and compress the artery against the sternum). Takayasu arteritis and atherosclerosis of the trunk cause an absent right radial pulse and right-sided ischemic symptoms; the right subclavian steal starts here.

name: Ascending cervical artery
function: Small branch of the inferior thyroid artery that climbs the prevertebral muscles medial to the phrenic nerve, supplying the deep neck muscles and sending spinal branches into the intervertebral foramina.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Inferior thyroid artery as it turns medially, or directly from the thyrocervical trunk.

details.label: Course
details.value: Ascends on the anterior tubercles of the cervical transverse processes between the anterior scalene and longus capitis, parallel and medial to the phrenic nerve.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Muscular branches to the longus colli, longus capitis and scalene muscles; spinal branches through the intervertebral foramina to the vertebral bodies, meninges and cord, anastomosing with the vertebral and deep cervical arteries.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Prevertebral and scalene muscles (Netter muscle tables p221–222), cervical vertebrae and the spinal cord via radicular branches.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Phrenic nerve runs lateral to it on the anterior scalene; the sympathetic trunk and middle cervical ganglion lie medial on the longus colli.

pearl: A landmark for the phrenic nerve on the anterior scalene during neck dissection and anterior cervical spine surgery, and a collateral route to the cervical cord and vertebral artery when the vertebral artery is occluded; its radicular branches can be the source of a cervical epidural hematoma or a feeder of a spinal dural fistula.

name: Dorsal scapular artery
function: Artery to the rhomboids and levator scapulae that runs along the medial border of the scapula; it arises either as the deep branch of the transverse cervical artery or directly from the third part of the subclavian artery, passing through the brachial plexus.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Second or third part of the subclavian artery in most people, passing between the trunks of the brachial plexus; in about 30% it shares a common origin with the superficial cervical artery from the transverse cervical artery, as its deep branch.

details.label: Course
details.value: Runs posteriorly through the brachial plexus and under the levator scapulae to the superior angle of the scapula, then descends along the medial border deep to the rhomboids with the dorsal scapular nerve.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Muscular branches to the rhomboids, levator scapulae and trapezius; anastomoses with the suprascapular, circumflex scapular and posterior intercostal arteries around the scapula.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Rhomboid major and minor, levator scapulae and the lower trapezius; contributes to the scapular anastomosis.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Travels with the dorsal scapular nerve (C5); the superficial branch of the transverse cervical artery supplies the trapezius above it.

pearl: Part of the scapular anastomosis (with the suprascapular and circumflex scapular arteries) that keeps the arm perfused when the axillary artery is blocked between the thyrocervical trunk and the subscapular artery. It runs with the dorsal scapular nerve, so both are at risk in posterior triangle surgery and in a middle scalene hematoma.

name: Deep cervical and supreme intercostal arteries (costocervical trunk)
function: The two branches of the costocervical trunk: the deep cervical artery ascends in the back of the neck between the semispinalis muscles, the supreme (highest) intercostal artery descends over the neck of the first rib to supply the first two intercostal spaces.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Costocervical trunk from the posterior surface of the subclavian artery (second part on the right, first part on the left), which divides over the pleural cupola.

details.label: Course
details.value: Deep cervical artery passes backward above the neck of the first rib, between the transverse process of C7 and the first rib, and ascends between semispinalis capitis and semispinalis cervicis; the supreme intercostal artery descends in front of the necks of the first and second ribs.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Deep cervical: muscular branches and spinal branches into the intervertebral foramina, anastomosing with the descending branch of the occipital artery and the vertebral artery. Supreme intercostal: first and second posterior intercostal arteries.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Deep posterior neck muscles (semispinalis, splenius, suboccipital muscles), cervical vertebrae and spinal cord branches; upper two intercostal spaces, their muscles and the upper thoracic cord.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Sympathetic trunk and stellate ganglion lie medial to the supreme intercostal artery on the neck of the first rib; the deep cervical artery is the posterior counterpart of the vertebral artery.

pearl: The deep cervical and occipital arteries form the main collateral to the vertebral artery when the subclavian or proximal vertebral is occluded (subclavian steal). The supreme intercostal artery and stellate ganglion sit on the neck of the first rib, where they are at risk in first-rib resection for thoracic outlet syndrome and in Pancoast tumors.

name: Ascending palatine artery
function: First branch of the facial artery in the neck; climbs between the styloglossus and stylopharyngeus on the pharyngeal wall to supply the soft palate, palatine tonsil and auditory tube.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Facial artery near its origin from the external carotid, in the carotid triangle.

details.label: Course
details.value: Ascends on the lateral pharyngeal wall between the styloglossus and stylopharyngeus, then crosses over the upper border of the superior pharyngeal constrictor to reach the soft palate; a branch passes with the levator veli palatini.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Tonsillar branches to the palatine tonsil (one of the five tonsillar sources on Netter Plate 72), branches to the soft palate anastomosing with the lesser palatine artery, branches to the auditory tube and superior constrictor, glandular branches.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Soft palate and palatal muscles (levator veli palatini, musculus uvulae, palatopharyngeus), palatine tonsil, upper pharynx and auditory tube (Netter muscle tables).

details.label: Relations
details.value: Runs with the ascending pharyngeal artery and the pharyngeal plexus on the constrictors; the internal carotid lies posterolateral.

pearl: One of the vessels that bleeds after tonsillectomy (with the tonsillar branch and the lesser palatine artery); secondary hemorrhage at 5–10 days is from slough separating over these vessels. Peritonsillar abscess drainage stays medial to avoid the internal carotid behind the ascending palatine territory.

name: Submental artery
function: Largest cervical branch of the facial artery; runs forward on the mylohyoid beneath the chin, supplying the submandibular gland, the floor-of-mouth muscles and the chin, and anastomosing with the inferior alveolar and mental arteries.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Facial artery as it leaves the submandibular gland, just before it curls over the mandible.

details.label: Course
details.value: Runs forward on the inferior surface of the mylohyoid, below the body of the mandible, deep to the anterior belly of digastric, to the chin.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Muscular branches to mylohyoid and the anterior belly of digastric, glandular branches to the submandibular gland, a superficial branch to the chin skin and a deep branch that pierces the mylohyoid to anastomose with the sublingual artery; terminal branches join the mental and inferior labial arteries.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Anterior belly of digastric, mylohyoid, submandibular gland, skin of the chin and submental region, and with the sublingual artery the floor of the mouth and platysma (Netter muscle tables p219–222).

details.label: Relations
details.value: Submental vein and lymph nodes accompany it; the nerve to mylohyoid runs with it on the muscle.

pearl: The submental artery is the pedicle of the submental island flap used to reconstruct the floor of mouth and lower face, and it is ligated in level I neck dissection. In Ludwig angina the submental space it supplies becomes board-hard, and its bleeding complicates drainage.

name: Lateral nasal artery (with alar branches)
function: Branch of the facial artery to the ala and dorsum of the nose, given off beside the ala before the facial artery ends as the angular artery; its alar branches anastomose with the external nasal and septal arteries.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Facial artery at the level of the ala of the nose.

details.label: Course
details.value: Runs medially across the ala and up the side of the nose beneath the nasalis muscle.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Alar branches to the ala, nasal tip and columella, anastomosing with the external (dorsal) nasal branch of the ophthalmic artery, the nasal septal branch of the superior labial artery and the anterior ethmoidal artery.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Skin and cartilage of the ala and lower dorsum of the nose, nasal vestibule and the nasalis and levator labii superioris alaeque nasi muscles.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Angular artery continues from it to the medial canthus; the external nasal vein and nasalis overlie it.

pearl: The lateral nasal and superior labial branches of the facial artery are part of the anastomosis in the nasal vestibule (with anterior ethmoidal and sphenopalatine branches) that is the usual site of anterior epistaxis (Netter Table 2.2). Alar necrosis after filler injection or a prolonged nasal cannula follows occlusion of these alar branches.

name: Descending (greater) palatine artery and lesser palatine arteries
function: Branch of the third part of the maxillary artery that descends in the greater palatine canal and divides into the greater palatine artery to the hard palate and the lesser palatine arteries to the soft palate and tonsil.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Third (pterygopalatine) part of the maxillary artery in the pterygopalatine fossa.

details.label: Course
details.value: Descends in the greater palatine canal with the greater and lesser palatine nerves; the greater palatine artery emerges through the greater palatine foramen medial to the third molar and runs forward in a groove to the incisive canal, the lesser palatine arteries leave through the lesser palatine foramina in the pyramidal process.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Greater palatine artery (see its own card): branches to the hard palate mucosa, palatal gingiva and the anastomosis with the sphenopalatine artery in the incisive canal; lesser palatine arteries to the soft palate and palatine tonsil; posterior inferior nasal branches through the perpendicular plate to the inferior concha.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Hard palate and palatal gingiva, soft palate and uvula (with the ascending palatine artery), palatine tonsil (one of its five tonsillar sources), inferior meatus mucosa (Netter muscle tables: musculus uvulae and palatal muscles).

details.label: Relations
details.value: Maxillary sinus lateral to the canal; the greater palatine nerve accompanies it.

pearl: The greater palatine foramen is the injection site for a greater palatine block and for transpalatal control of posterior epistaxis; the lesser palatine arteries bleed after tonsillectomy and adenoidectomy. The palatal flap for cleft repair is raised on the greater palatine pedicle, which must be spared.

name: Posterior superior alveolar artery
function: Branch of the third part of the maxillary artery that descends on the maxillary tuberosity and enters the posterior superior alveolar foramina to supply the molars, premolars, gingiva and the lining of the maxillary sinus.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Maxillary artery as it enters the pterygopalatine fossa, often by a common trunk with the infraorbital artery.

details.label: Course
details.value: Descends on the infratemporal surface of the maxilla with the posterior superior alveolar nerve; branches enter the posterior superior alveolar foramina above the tuberosity, others continue down to the gingiva.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Dental branches to the molar and premolar roots, alveolar branches to the bone and gingiva, and branches to the mucosa of the maxillary sinus that anastomose with the infraorbital artery's anterior and middle superior alveolar branches.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Maxillary molars and premolars, their periodontium and buccal gingiva, the posterolateral wall and mucosa of the maxillary sinus.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Pterygoid venous plexus and buccal fat pad lie lateral; the sinus wall is thin here.

pearl: The posterior superior alveolar block is placed at the maxillary tuberosity; advancing too far pierces the pterygoid plexus and this artery, giving a rapidly expanding cheek hematoma. The artery also bleeds in Le Fort I osteotomy and in sinus-lift bone grafts, where it crosses the lateral sinus wall.

name: Deep temporal, masseteric, pterygoid and buccal arteries (2nd-part maxillary branches)
function: Branches of the second (pterygoid) part of the maxillary artery that supply the muscles of mastication and the cheek, each travelling with the corresponding branch of the mandibular nerve.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Second part of the maxillary artery as it crosses the lateral pterygoid muscle in the infratemporal fossa.

details.label: Course
details.value: Anterior and posterior deep temporal arteries ascend between temporalis and the skull; the masseteric artery passes laterally through the mandibular notch with the masseteric nerve; the pterygoid arteries are short branches to the medial and lateral pterygoids; the buccal artery runs forward with the buccal nerve onto the buccinator.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Deep temporal arteries anastomose with the middle temporal (superficial temporal) and lacrimal arteries; the masseteric artery joins the transverse facial artery; the buccal artery anastomoses with the facial and infraorbital arteries.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Temporalis (deep temporal), masseter (masseteric), medial and lateral pterygoids (pterygoid), buccinator and cheek mucosa and skin (buccal) — the blood-supply column of the mastication rows in Netter's muscle tables.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Each artery accompanies the nerve of the same name from the anterior division of V3; the pterygoid venous plexus surrounds them.

pearl: Hemorrhage and trismus after mandibular ramus fractures or sagittal split osteotomy come from these muscular branches in the masticator space. The deep temporal arteries supply the temporalis flap used for orbital and palate reconstruction; the buccal artery pedicle supports buccal fat pad flaps for oroantral fistula closure.

name: Accessory meningeal artery
function: Small branch of the maxillary (or middle meningeal) artery that enters the skull through the foramen ovale to supply the trigeminal ganglion and the dura of the middle cranial fossa, after giving most of its branches to the pterygoid muscles and tensor veli palatini outside the skull.

details.label: Origin
details.value: First part of the maxillary artery or the middle meningeal artery near its origin.

details.label: Course
details.value: Ascends medial to the lateral pterygoid and passes through the foramen ovale with the mandibular nerve and the lesser petrosal nerve.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Extracranial branches to the medial and lateral pterygoids, tensor veli palatini, auditory tube and the otic ganglion region; intracranial branches to the trigeminal ganglion, the dura around the cavernous sinus and the floor of the middle cranial fossa.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Pterygoid muscles and tensor veli palatini (the larger part of its territory), trigeminal ganglion and adjacent dura; anastomoses with the cavernous branches of the internal carotid.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Foramen ovale contents: V3, accessory meningeal artery, lesser petrosal nerve and emissary veins.

pearl: Its dural branches explain why a meningioma or dural arteriovenous fistula of the middle fossa may be fed through the foramen ovale, and why embolization of the maxillary artery for epistaxis must avoid reflux through accessory meningeal to internal carotid anastomoses (risk of cranial nerve palsy or stroke).

name: Deep auricular and anterior tympanic arteries
function: The first two branches of the maxillary artery, arising behind the temporomandibular joint: the deep auricular artery pierces the floor of the external acoustic meatus to supply the meatus and the outer tympanic membrane, the anterior tympanic artery passes through the petrotympanic fissure to the middle ear.

details.label: Origin
details.value: First (mandibular) part of the maxillary artery behind the neck of the mandible, often by a common stem.

details.label: Course
details.value: Deep auricular: ascends in the parotid behind the TMJ and pierces the cartilaginous or bony wall of the external acoustic meatus. Anterior tympanic: runs up behind the TMJ and enters the tympanic cavity through the petrotympanic fissure with the chorda tympani.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Deep auricular: twigs to the TMJ capsule, meatal skin and the outer layer of the tympanic membrane. Anterior tympanic: branches to the tympanic membrane (arteries of the mallear stria) and the marginal arterial rete on the membrane, anastomosing with the stylomastoid, caroticotympanic and superior tympanic arteries.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: External acoustic meatus and outer tympanic membrane, temporomandibular joint, and the mucosa and ossicles of the anterior tympanic cavity.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Auriculotemporal nerve and superficial temporal vessels lie lateral; the chorda tympani shares the petrotympanic fissure.

pearl: Together with the stylomastoid branch these form the vascular ring of the tympanic membrane seen as the 'marginal rete'; their engorgement gives the injected drum of early otitis media and brisk bleeding from meatal lacerations. The deep auricular artery can be injured in TMJ arthroscopy.

name: Artery of the pterygoid canal and pharyngeal artery (3rd-part maxillary branches)
function: Two small posterior branches of the third part of the maxillary artery: the artery of the pterygoid canal (vidian artery) runs back through the canal to the auditory tube and nasopharynx, the pharyngeal artery through the pharyngeal (palatovaginal) canal to the roof of the nasopharynx and sphenoid sinus.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Third part of the maxillary artery in the pterygopalatine fossa; the vidian artery can also arise from the petrous internal carotid, which it meets in the canal.

details.label: Course
details.value: Artery of the pterygoid canal passes backward through the pterygoid canal with the vidian nerve to the region of the foramen lacerum; the pharyngeal artery runs backward through the pharyngeal canal between the sphenoid body and the palatine bone.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Vidian: branches to the auditory tube, upper pharynx and tympanic cavity, anastomosing with the petrous internal carotid (an internal-to-external carotid anastomosis). Pharyngeal: branches to the sphenoid sinus, auditory tube and nasopharyngeal roof.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Mucosa of the nasopharynx, auditory tube, sphenoid sinus and the pterygopalatine ganglion region.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Nerve of the pterygoid canal accompanies the vidian artery; the sphenopalatine artery leaves the fossa medially just above.

pearl: The vidian artery is a feeder of juvenile nasopharyngeal angiofibroma and a dangerous collateral between the maxillary and internal carotid arteries during embolization for epistaxis; identifying the vidian canal guides endoscopic surgeons to the petrous carotid at the foramen lacerum.

name: Stylomastoid artery
function: Branch of the posterior auricular (sometimes occipital) artery that enters the stylomastoid foramen alongside the facial nerve and runs up the facial canal to supply the nerve, the stapedius, the mastoid air cells and the posterior tympanic cavity.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Posterior auricular artery just below the stylomastoid foramen.

details.label: Course
details.value: Ascends through the stylomastoid foramen with the facial nerve, within the facial canal, to the posterior wall of the middle ear.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Posterior tympanic artery to the tympanic membrane and marginal rete, stapedial branch to the stapedius muscle and stapes, mastoid branches to the mastoid antrum and cells, and branches to the facial nerve and semicircular canals.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Facial nerve in its vertical and tympanic segments, stapedius, posterior tympanic membrane and cavity, mastoid air cells, part of the bony labyrinth.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Facial nerve, chorda tympani origin and the pyramidal eminence lie beside it in the canal; the petrosal branch of the middle meningeal artery supplies the upper facial canal.

pearl: The facial nerve's blood supply in the narrow facial canal comes from this artery and the petrosal branch of the middle meningeal: ischemia and oedema in the labyrinthine segment underlie Bell palsy, and the stylomastoid foramen is where the nerve is identified in parotid surgery. The artery bleeds during mastoidectomy near the facial ridge.

name: Lacrimal artery
function: Early branch of the ophthalmic artery that runs along the upper border of the lateral rectus to the lacrimal gland, continuing to the lateral eyelids and conjunctiva; its recurrent meningeal branch anastomoses with the middle meningeal artery through the superior orbital fissure.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Ophthalmic artery just after it enters the orbit, lateral to the optic nerve.

details.label: Course
details.value: Passes forward with the lacrimal nerve along the upper border of the lateral rectus to the lacrimal gland, then pierces the orbital septum to the lateral eyelids.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Glandular branches to the lacrimal gland; superior and inferior lateral palpebral arteries forming the palpebral arcades with the medial palpebral arteries; zygomatic branches (zygomaticofacial and zygomaticotemporal) to the cheek and temple; recurrent meningeal branch back through the superior orbital fissure to the dura; muscular branches to lateral rectus and the anterior ciliary arteries.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Lacrimal gland, lateral parts of both eyelids and conjunctiva, lateral rectus, skin over the zygoma and temple, dura of the middle cranial fossa.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Lacrimal nerve (V1) runs with it; the recurrent meningeal anastomosis is a route for the external carotid to feed the orbit when the ophthalmic artery is occluded.

pearl: The recurrent meningeal branch is an internal–external carotid anastomosis through the superior orbital fissure, a collateral in carotid occlusion and an embolization hazard in middle meningeal artery embolization for chronic subdural hematoma. Lacrimal gland tumors and dacryoadenitis are supplied by it.

name: Posterior ethmoidal artery
function: Small branch of the ophthalmic artery that leaves the orbit through the posterior ethmoidal foramen to supply the posterior ethmoidal cells, the sphenoid sinus, the dura of the anterior cranial fossa and the upper posterior nasal septum.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Ophthalmic artery on the medial side of the orbit, proximal to the anterior ethmoidal artery.

details.label: Course
details.value: Passes medially between the superior oblique and medial rectus to the posterior ethmoidal foramen, through the posterior ethmoidal canal into the anterior cranial fossa beside the cribriform plate, then down into the nasal cavity.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Branches to the posterior ethmoidal cells and sphenoidal sinus, meningeal branches to the anterior fossa dura, septal and lateral nasal branches to the superior part of the septum and superior concha.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Posterior ethmoidal and sphenoid sinus mucosa, posterosuperior nasal septum and lateral wall, dura of the anterior cranial fossa.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Optic canal lies just behind the posterior ethmoidal foramen; the posterior ethmoidal nerve and vein accompany it.

pearl: The posterior ethmoidal foramen is the surgeon's warning line a few millimetres in front of the optic nerve on the medial orbital wall; the artery is ligated after the anterior ethmoidal in refractory superior epistaxis, taking care not to injure the optic nerve. With the anterior ethmoidal it supplies the olfactory region, the bleeding site in anterior fossa fractures.

name: Long and short posterior ciliary arteries and anterior ciliary arteries
function: Branches of the ophthalmic artery to the eyeball itself: the short posterior ciliary arteries supply the choroid and optic nerve head, the long posterior ciliary arteries run forward to the ciliary body and iris, and the anterior ciliary arteries reach the iris and conjunctiva along the rectus tendons.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Posterior ciliary arteries from the ophthalmic artery as it crosses the optic nerve; anterior ciliary arteries from the muscular branches to the four recti.

details.label: Course
details.value: Short posterior ciliary (10–20) pierce the sclera around the optic nerve into the choroid; two long posterior ciliary arteries pierce the sclera on either side of the nerve and run forward in the suprachoroidal space to the ciliary body; anterior ciliary arteries travel on the recti, pierce the sclera near the limbus and send recurrent branches back into the choroid.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Short posterior ciliary: choriocapillaris, circle of Zinn–Haller around the optic disc. Long posterior and anterior ciliary: major arterial circle of the iris, minor arterial circle, ciliary muscle and processes, episcleral and conjunctival branches.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Choroid and outer retina (photoreceptors), prelaminar optic nerve head, ciliary body and muscle, iris including sphincter and dilator pupillae, sclera, episclera and conjunctiva (Netter muscle tables: ciliary muscle and pupillary muscles by the ophthalmic artery).

details.label: Relations
details.value: Short and long ciliary nerves accompany the posterior ciliary arteries; the vorticose veins drain the same choroid.

pearl: Giant cell arteritis causes anterior ischemic optic neuropathy by occluding the short posterior ciliary arteries (pale swollen disc, sudden painless vision loss; start high-dose steroids before biopsy). Detaching more than two recti at once in strabismus surgery removes their anterior ciliary arteries and causes anterior segment ischemia. Central retinal artery occlusion spares the choroid, giving the cherry-red macula over an intact choroidal circulation.

name: External (dorsal) nasal artery
function: One of the two terminal branches of the ophthalmic artery; leaves the orbit above the medial palpebral ligament to supply the root and dorsum of the nose and the lacrimal sac, anastomosing with the angular artery of the facial system.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Terminal division of the ophthalmic artery at the medial orbital margin, with the supratrochlear artery.

details.label: Course
details.value: Pierces the orbital septum above the medial palpebral ligament, gives a branch to the lacrimal sac and runs down the side of the nasal dorsum with the external nasal branch of the anterior ethmoidal nerve.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Branch to the lacrimal sac, branches to the nasal dorsum and root, anastomosis with the angular artery (facial) and with the lateral nasal and anterior ethmoidal arteries.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Skin of the root and dorsum of the nose, lacrimal sac, and the medial canthal region.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Angular vein and artery lie beside it at the medial canthus; this is one of the marked internal–external carotid anastomoses on Netter Plate 99.

pearl: The dorsal nasal–angular anastomosis is why retrograde flow fills the ophthalmic artery when the internal carotid is occluded (and why a facial pulse can be felt at the medial canthus), and why filler injected into the nasal dorsum or glabella can reach the ophthalmic and central retinal arteries, causing blindness.

name: Branches of the lingual artery (suprahyoid, dorsal lingual, sublingual, deep lingual)
function: The four named branches of the lingual artery along its course under the hyoglossus: the suprahyoid branch to the hyoid muscles, the dorsal lingual arteries to the back of the tongue and tonsil, the sublingual artery to the floor of the mouth and sublingual gland, and the deep lingual artery, its terminal part in the tongue tip.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Lingual artery: first part above the hyoid (suprahyoid branch), second part deep to hyoglossus (dorsal lingual arteries), third part at the anterior border of hyoglossus (sublingual and deep lingual arteries).

details.label: Course
details.value: Suprahyoid branch runs along the upper border of the hyoid; dorsal lingual arteries ascend medial to hyoglossus to the dorsum and tonsil; the sublingual artery runs forward above the mylohyoid between genioglossus and the sublingual gland; the deep lingual artery runs under the ventral tongue mucosa beside the frenulum to the tip, where it anastomoses with its fellow.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Dorsal lingual: branches to the lingual tonsil, palatine tonsil, soft palate and epiglottis (a tonsillar source on Netter Plate 72). Sublingual: branches to the sublingual gland, mylohyoid, floor of mouth and gingiva, anastomosing with the submental artery through mylohyoid.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Hyoid muscles, intrinsic and extrinsic tongue muscles (Netter muscle tables credit genioglossus, hyoglossus, styloglossus and the intrinsic muscles to the lingual artery), lingual tonsil, sublingual gland, mylohyoid and the floor of the mouth.

details.label: Relations
details.value: The hypoglossal nerve and its vena comitans run superficial (lateral) to hyoglossus while the lingual artery passes deep to it; the lingual veins accompany each branch.

pearl: The deep lingual artery is visible under the thin ventral mucosa, so a tongue laceration or a biopsy of the ventral tongue bleeds briskly; tongue-base bleeding after tonsillectomy or in base-of-tongue cancer may need lingual artery ligation at the greater horn of the hyoid, where the hypoglossal nerve must be spared. Sublingual branches supply ranulas and bleed in floor-of-mouth surgery.

name: Superior laryngeal, cricothyroid and infrahyoid arteries (superior thyroid branches)
function: Branches of the superior thyroid artery to the larynx: the superior laryngeal artery pierces the thyrohyoid membrane with the internal laryngeal nerve to supply the supraglottic larynx, the cricothyroid artery crosses the median cricothyroid ligament, and the infrahyoid branch runs along the hyoid.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Superior thyroid artery in the carotid triangle, below the greater horn of the hyoid.

details.label: Course
details.value: Superior laryngeal artery runs medially deep to thyrohyoid and pierces the thyrohyoid membrane with the internal branch of the superior laryngeal nerve; the cricothyroid artery runs along the upper border of the cricothyroid muscle across the median cricothyroid ligament; the infrahyoid branch runs along the lower border of the hyoid.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Superior laryngeal: branches to the epiglottis, aryepiglottic folds, vestibular folds, piriform recess and the laryngeal muscles above the folds, anastomosing with the inferior laryngeal artery. Cricothyroid: anastomoses with its fellow in front of the ligament and supplies cricothyroid and the subglottis. Infrahyoid: infrahyoid muscles and hyoid.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Supraglottic and glottic larynx including the thyroarytenoid, vocalis, arytenoid and aryepiglottic muscles (Netter muscle tables: superior and inferior thyroid arteries), the cricothyroid muscle, the infrahyoid strap muscles.

details.label: Relations
details.value: External laryngeal nerve runs with the superior thyroid artery and must be separated from it before ligation; the cricothyroid artery crosses the cricothyrotomy site.

pearl: In cricothyrotomy the cricothyroid arteries cross the upper part of the median cricothyroid ligament, so the incision is kept low and horizontal. Laryngeal cancer surgery and supraglottic laryngectomy ligate the superior laryngeal pedicle at the thyrohyoid membrane; the external laryngeal nerve hugs the superior thyroid artery, so ligate the artery on the thyroid capsule to protect high-pitch voice.

name: Inferior laryngeal artery
function: Branch of the inferior thyroid artery that ascends with the recurrent laryngeal nerve behind the cricothyroid joint to supply the subglottic larynx and the laryngeal muscles, anastomosing with the superior laryngeal artery.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Inferior thyroid artery (thyrocervical trunk) near the lower pole of the thyroid.

details.label: Course
details.value: Ascends in the tracheoesophageal groove with the recurrent laryngeal nerve, passes deep to the inferior pharyngeal constrictor behind the cricothyroid joint and enters the larynx below the cricoid.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Branches to the posterior and lateral cricoarytenoid, thyroarytenoid and arytenoid muscles, the subglottic mucosa and the upper trachea; anastomoses with the superior laryngeal and cricothyroid arteries.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Infraglottic larynx, posterior laryngeal muscles and the mucosa below the vocal folds (Netter muscle tables list the inferior thyroid artery for the intrinsic laryngeal muscles).

details.label: Relations
details.value: Recurrent laryngeal nerve accompanies it; both cross the inferior thyroid artery near the thyroid lobe, where the nerve may pass in front of, behind or between the artery's branches.

pearl: The recurrent laryngeal nerve travels with this artery, so in thyroidectomy the inferior thyroid artery branches are ligated individually on the capsule, not in bulk, to protect the nerve and the parathyroid supply (Netter Table 2.2). Subglottic edema (croup, post-intubation) is in this artery's territory, the narrowest part of the pediatric airway.

name: Mental and mylohyoid branches of the inferior alveolar artery
function: The two branches of the inferior alveolar artery outside the mandibular canal: the mylohyoid branch leaves before the mandibular foramen to run with the nerve to mylohyoid on the floor of the mouth, and the mental branch exits the mental foramen with the mental nerve to the chin and lower lip.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Inferior alveolar artery (first part of the maxillary artery): the mylohyoid branch arises just above the mandibular foramen, the mental branch is the terminal branch leaving the mandibular canal at the mental foramen.

details.label: Course
details.value: Mylohyoid branch pierces the sphenomandibular ligament, runs in the mylohyoid groove of the mandible with the nerve to mylohyoid and spreads on the inferior surface of the mylohyoid; the mental branch emerges below the premolars and fans into the chin.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Mylohyoid: muscular branches to mylohyoid and the anterior belly of digastric, anastomosing with the submental artery. Mental: branches to the chin skin, lower lip and labial gingiva, anastomosing with the inferior labial and submental arteries; the incisive branch continues in the bone to the incisors.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Mylohyoid and anterior digastric (with the submental and sublingual arteries, Netter muscle tables), skin and mucosa of the chin and lower lip, labial gingiva of the incisors and canines.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Nerve to mylohyoid and mental nerve accompany each branch; the mental foramen lies below the second premolar in line with the supraorbital and infraorbital foramina.

pearl: The mental foramen is the landmark for the mental nerve block and the structure to avoid in genioplasty and implant placement; a severely resorbed edentulous mandible brings the foramen and vessels to the alveolar crest. Bleeding from the mylohyoid branch and lingual perforation during implant drilling can cause a floor-of-mouth hematoma that threatens the airway.

name: Cervical part of internal carotid artery
function: First part of the internal carotid, carrying blood from the carotid bifurcation to the skull base without giving any branch.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Carotid bifurcation at the upper border of the thyroid cartilage (C4).

details.label: Course
details.value: Ascends in the carotid sheath, first lateral then posteromedial to the external carotid, to the external opening of the carotid canal.

details.label: Branches
details.value: None in the neck.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: No cervical structures; all flow continues to the brain and orbit.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Internal jugular vein lateral, vagus nerve posterolateral, sympathetic trunk behind; crossed laterally by the hypoglossal nerve, occipital artery and posterior belly of digastric; styloid muscles and glossopharyngeal nerve pass between it and the external carotid.

pearl: Atherosclerotic plaque at its origin is the classic source of emboli causing amaurosis fugax and anterior-circulation TIA or stroke; cervical dissection gives neck pain with a painful Horner syndrome.

name: Petrous part of internal carotid artery
function: Second part of the internal carotid, running through the carotid canal of the temporal bone.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Continuation of the cervical part at the external opening of the carotid canal.

details.label: Course
details.value: Ascends, then bends anteromedially in the carotid canal in front of the tympanic cavity and cochlea, and passes above the cartilage filling the foramen lacerum to enter the cavernous sinus.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Caroticotympanic artery (to the tympanic cavity) and artery of the pterygoid canal (an internal-to-external carotid anastomosis).

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Tympanic cavity; anastomotic supply toward the pterygopalatine fossa.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Surrounded by the internal carotid sympathetic plexus and a venous plexus; the auditory tube and tensor tympani lie anterolateral, the trigeminal ganglion above its roof.

pearl: A thin or dehiscent bony wall lets carotid pulsation be heard as pulsatile tinnitus and puts the artery at risk in middle-ear surgery.

name: Cavernous part of internal carotid artery
function: Third part of the internal carotid, forming the S-shaped carotid siphon inside the cavernous sinus and supplying the pituitary, nearby dura and cranial nerves.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Continuation of the petrous part above the foramen lacerum.

details.label: Course
details.value: Runs forward in the carotid sulcus on the side of the sphenoid body within the cavernous sinus, then turns up medial to the anterior clinoid process to pierce the dural roof.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Meningohypophyseal trunk (tentorial branch, dorsal meningeal artery, inferior hypophyseal artery); artery to the inferior cavernous sinus (inferolateral trunk) with a branch to the superior orbital fissure; recurrent artery of foramen lacerum; branches to foramen rotundum, foramen ovale and foramen spinosum; meningeal and cavernous branches.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Neurohypophysis, dura of the tentorium and clivus, trigeminal ganglion and the nerves in the cavernous sinus wall.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Abducens nerve lies directly lateral to it inside the sinus; oculomotor, trochlear, ophthalmic and maxillary nerves lie in the lateral wall; the hypophysis is medial.

pearl: Rupture here produces a carotid-cavernous fistula with pulsating exophthalmos, chemosis, an orbital bruit and ophthalmoplegia.

name: Cerebral part of internal carotid artery
function: Terminal, intradural part of the internal carotid that gives the ophthalmic artery and the anterior circulation of the brain.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Continuation of the cavernous part after it pierces the dura medial to the anterior clinoid process.

details.label: Course
details.value: Runs back and up below the optic nerve, lateral to the optic chiasm, to the anterior perforated substance where it divides.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Ophthalmic artery, superior hypophyseal arteries, posterior communicating artery, anterior choroidal artery; terminal anterior cerebral and middle cerebral arteries.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Orbit and retina, pituitary stalk and adenohypophysis (via the portal system), optic chiasm and tract, internal capsule, and most of the cerebral hemisphere.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Optic nerve above and medial, oculomotor nerve lateral, anterior clinoid process lateral.

pearl: An aneurysm at the origin of the posterior communicating artery compresses the oculomotor nerve, giving a painful third-nerve palsy with a dilated pupil.

name: Mandibular (first) part of maxillary artery
function: First part of the maxillary artery, whose branches all enter bone to supply the ear, the dura and the mandibular teeth.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Larger terminal branch of the external carotid in the parotid gland behind the neck of the mandible.

details.label: Course
details.value: Runs horizontally forward between the neck of the mandible and the sphenomandibular ligament, along the lower border of lateral pterygoid.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Deep auricular artery, anterior tympanic artery, middle meningeal artery, accessory meningeal artery, inferior alveolar artery (with its mylohyoid branch).

details.label: Supplies
details.value: External acoustic meatus and tympanic membrane, TMJ, dura and calvaria, mandible, lower teeth and chin.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Auriculotemporal nerve lies above; its two roots encircle the middle meningeal artery; maxillary veins accompany it.

pearl: Every branch of this part passes through a foramen or canal, a useful rule for recalling them.

name: Pterygoid (second) part of maxillary artery
function: Second part of the maxillary artery, whose branches are all muscular and supply the muscles of mastication and the buccinator region.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Continuation of the mandibular part at the lower border of lateral pterygoid.

details.label: Course
details.value: Runs obliquely forward and up, superficial or deep to the lower head of lateral pterygoid, toward the pterygomaxillary fissure.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Anterior and posterior deep temporal arteries, masseteric artery, medial and lateral pterygoid arteries, buccal artery.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Temporalis, masseter, medial and lateral pterygoids, buccinator and cheek.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Lies within the pterygoid venous plexus; the buccal, lingual and inferior alveolar nerves are close to it.

pearl: Bleeding from this part and the surrounding pterygoid plexus causes the hematoma that can follow a posterior superior alveolar nerve block.

name: Pterygopalatine (third) part of maxillary artery
function: Third part of the maxillary artery, distributing with the branches of the maxillary nerve to the nasal cavity, palate, upper teeth and face.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Continuation of the pterygoid part as it passes between the two heads of lateral pterygoid.

details.label: Course
details.value: Enters the pterygopalatine fossa through the pterygomaxillary fissure and breaks up in front of the pterygopalatine ganglion.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Posterior superior alveolar artery, infraorbital artery (with middle and anterior superior alveolar arteries), descending palatine artery (greater and lesser palatine arteries), artery of the pterygoid canal, pharyngeal artery, sphenopalatine artery (terminal).

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Maxillary teeth and sinus, lower eyelid and cheek, hard and soft palate, nasopharynx, nasal septum and lateral nasal wall.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Lies anterior to the pterygopalatine ganglion and the maxillary nerve in the fossa.

pearl: Its sphenopalatine terminal branch is the vessel clipped or embolized for refractory posterior epistaxis.

name: First part of subclavian artery
function: Segment of the subclavian medial to the anterior scalene that gives the vertebral, internal thoracic and thyrocervical vessels.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Right: brachiocephalic trunk behind the sternoclavicular joint. Left: aortic arch.

details.label: Course
details.value: Arches up and laterally over the cervical pleura to the medial border of the anterior scalene.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Vertebral artery, internal thoracic artery, thyrocervical trunk (inferior thyroid, transverse cervical, suprascapular arteries).

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Brain stem and cerebellum, anterior chest wall, thyroid gland, root of the neck and scapular region.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Crossed anteriorly by the vagus and phrenic nerves and the internal jugular and vertebral veins; the ansa subclavia loops around it; the right recurrent laryngeal nerve hooks beneath it; the thoracic duct crosses the left one.

pearl: Stenosis proximal to the vertebral origin causes subclavian steal: arm exercise reverses vertebral flow and produces vertebrobasilar symptoms with a lower blood pressure in that arm.

name: Second part of subclavian artery
function: Short highest segment of the subclavian lying behind the anterior scalene, giving the costocervical trunk.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Continuation of the first part at the medial border of the anterior scalene.

details.label: Course
details.value: Forms the summit of the arch behind the anterior scalene, on the cervical pleura and suprapleural membrane.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Costocervical trunk (deep cervical and supreme intercostal arteries).

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Deep muscles of the back of the neck and the first two intercostal spaces.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Anterior scalene in front separates it from the subclavian vein and phrenic nerve; middle scalene and the lower trunk of the brachial plexus lie behind.

name: Third part of subclavian artery
function: Most superficial segment of the subclavian, crossing the first rib in the posterior triangle to become the axillary artery.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Continuation of the second part at the lateral border of the anterior scalene.

details.label: Course
details.value: Runs down and laterally across the posterior triangle and the upper surface of the first rib to its outer border.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Dorsal scapular artery when it is not the deep branch of the transverse cervical artery; often no branch.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Rhomboids and levator scapulae through the dorsal scapular artery; continues as the upper limb supply.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Trunks of the brachial plexus lie above and behind, the lower trunk directly behind on the first rib; subclavian vein in front and below; crossed by the suprascapular vessels.

pearl: Its pulse is felt, and it can be compressed against the first rib, in the angle between the clavicle and the posterior border of sternocleidomastoid; a cervical rib or tight scalene interval compresses it here in thoracic outlet syndrome.

name: Prevertebral part of vertebral artery (V1)
function: First part of the vertebral artery, from its subclavian origin to the transverse foramen of C6.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Posterosuperior aspect of the first part of the subclavian artery.

details.label: Course
details.value: Ascends in the angle between longus colli and the anterior scalene to enter the transverse foramen of C6.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Usually none.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: No territory of its own; carries flow toward the hindbrain.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Behind the common carotid artery and vertebral vein; crossed by the inferior thyroid artery (and the thoracic duct on the left); the cervicothoracic (stellate) ganglion lies behind it.

pearl: Its origin is the commonest site of vertebral atherosclerosis.

name: Cervical part of vertebral artery (V2)
function: Second part of the vertebral artery, ascending through the cervical transverse foramina and reinforcing the supply of the cervical cord.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Continuation of the prevertebral part at the transverse foramen of C6.

details.label: Course
details.value: Ascends through the transverse foramina of C6 to C1, in front of the anterior rami of the cervical nerves, with the vertebral venous plexus and sympathetic vertebral plexus.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Segmental medullary (spinal) branches through the intervertebral foramina; muscular branches to the deep neck muscles.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Cervical spinal cord and meninges, vertebrae and deep cervical muscles.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Uncovertebral joints lie medial; the C7 transverse foramen carries vertebral veins but usually not the artery.

pearl: Uncovertebral osteophytes or neck rotation can compress the artery within the transverse foramina, causing vertebrobasilar insufficiency.

name: Atlantic part of vertebral artery (V3, horizontal segment)
function: Third part of the vertebral artery, curving behind the lateral mass of the atlas in the suboccipital triangle.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Continuation of the cervical part as it leaves the transverse foramen of the atlas.

details.label: Course
details.value: Winds posteromedially in the groove for the vertebral artery on the posterior arch of the atlas, then pierces the posterior atlanto-occipital membrane and dura.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Muscular branches to the suboccipital muscles, anastomosing with the descending branch of the occipital artery and the deep cervical artery.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Suboccipital muscles.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Lies in the floor of the suboccipital triangle with the suboccipital nerve (posterior ramus of C1) between it and the posterior arch of the atlas.

pearl: This mobile loop is the usual site of vertebral artery dissection after sudden neck rotation or manipulation, a cause of posterior-circulation stroke in young adults.

name: Intracranial part of vertebral artery (V4)
function: Fourth, intradural part of the vertebral artery, supplying the medulla, upper cord and inferior cerebellum before forming the basilar artery.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Continuation of the atlantic part after it pierces the dura.

details.label: Course
details.value: Passes through the foramen magnum and runs up and medially in front of the medulla to the lower border of the pons, where it joins its fellow.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Anterior and posterior meningeal branches, posterior spinal artery, posterior inferior cerebellar artery, anterior spinal artery.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Medulla, upper cervical cord, inferior cerebellum and dura of the posterior cranial fossa.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Rootlets of the hypoglossal nerve lie behind it; the first denticulate ligament and the spinal accessory root are posterior.

pearl: Occlusion of this part, more often than of PICA itself, produces the lateral medullary (Wallenberg) syndrome.

name: Aortic arch
function: Arch of the aorta in the superior mediastinum, giving the three great vessels that supply the head, neck and upper limbs.

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Branches from right to left: brachiocephalic trunk, left common carotid artery, left subclavian artery. The aorta itself is labelled as ascending aorta, arch and descending aorta.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Continuation of the ascending aorta behind the right second sternocostal joint.

details.label: Course
details.value: Arches up, back and to the left over the root of the left lung, in front of and then to the left of the trachea, to the left side of T4.

details.label: Branches
details.value: In order: brachiocephalic trunk (to right common carotid and right subclavian), left common carotid artery, left subclavian artery; occasionally a thyroid ima artery.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Head, neck and both upper limbs through its three branches.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Left brachiocephalic vein crosses in front of its branches; left vagus and phrenic nerves cross its left side; the left recurrent laryngeal nerve hooks under it beside the ligamentum arteriosum.

pearl: An arch aneurysm can stretch the left recurrent laryngeal nerve and present with hoarseness.

name: Frontal branch of superficial temporal artery
function: Anterior terminal branch of the superficial temporal artery, supplying the temple and lateral forehead.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Division of the superficial temporal artery on the temporal fascia about 2-3 cm above the zygomatic arch.

details.label: Course
details.value: Runs tortuously forward and up across the temple toward the forehead in the superficial fascia.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Cutaneous and muscular twigs; anastomoses with the supraorbital and supratrochlear arteries and with its fellow.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Skin, frontalis and pericranium of the lateral forehead and anterior temple.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Runs with the temporal branches of the facial nerve and branches of the auriculotemporal nerve; the anastomosis with the supraorbital artery links external and internal carotid territories.

pearl: This is the visible, tortuous temple vessel that is tender and nodular in giant cell arteritis and is the usual site of temporal artery biopsy.

name: Parietal branch of superficial temporal artery
function: Posterior terminal branch of the superficial temporal artery, supplying the parietal scalp.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Division of the superficial temporal artery above the zygomatic arch.

details.label: Course
details.value: Ascends and curves backward over the temporal fascia and the side of the head.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Cutaneous twigs; anastomoses with its fellow across the vertex and with the posterior auricular and occipital arteries.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Skin and aponeurosis of the temporal and parietal scalp.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Lies in the dense connective tissue layer of the scalp with the auriculotemporal nerve.

pearl: Scalp arteries are held open by the dense connective tissue layer and anastomose freely, so scalp lacerations bleed briskly from both cut ends.

name: Frontal (anterior) branch of middle meningeal artery
function: Larger anterior division of the middle meningeal artery, supplying the anterior dura and inner table of the skull.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Division of the middle meningeal artery on the floor of the middle cranial fossa.

details.label: Course
details.value: Crosses the greater wing of the sphenoid, grooving or tunnelling the bone deep to the pterion, then ascends toward the vertex over the frontal and anterior parietal regions.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Branches to the dura, diploe and inner table; orbital (anastomotic) branch joining the recurrent meningeal branch of the lacrimal artery.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Dura and calvaria of the anterior and middle cranial fossae and frontoparietal convexity.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Lies between the dura and the bone immediately deep to the pterion, overlying the precentral region of the brain.

pearl: A fracture through the pterion tears this branch, producing an epidural hematoma with a lucid interval and a biconvex collection on CT.

name: Parietal (posterior) branch of middle meningeal artery
function: Posterior division of the middle meningeal artery, supplying the posterior dura and calvaria.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Division of the middle meningeal artery on the floor of the middle cranial fossa.

details.label: Course
details.value: Curves backward over the squamous part of the temporal bone and the parietal bone toward the lambda.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Branches to the dura, diploe and inner table; anastomoses with the mastoid branch of the occipital artery and its fellow.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Dura and calvaria of the posterior parietal and occipital convexity.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Runs extradurally in grooves on the squamous temporal and parietal bones.

name: Posterior lateral nasal branches of sphenopalatine artery
function: Branches of the sphenopalatine artery that supply most of the lateral wall of the nasal cavity.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Sphenopalatine artery as it enters the nasal cavity through the sphenopalatine foramen.

details.label: Course
details.value: Run forward over the middle and inferior nasal conchae and their meatuses.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Branches to the conchae and meatuses and to the maxillary, ethmoidal and sphenoidal sinuses; anastomose with the anterior lateral nasal branches of the anterior ethmoidal artery and the lateral nasal branch of the facial artery.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Mucosa of the lateral nasal wall, conchae and paranasal sinuses.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Accompany the posterior superior lateral nasal nerves from the pterygopalatine ganglion.

pearl: They are the usual source of posterior epistaxis, controlled by endoscopic sphenopalatine artery ligation behind the middle concha.

name: Posterior septal branches of sphenopalatine artery
function: Terminal branches of the sphenopalatine artery that supply the nasal septum and join the anterior septal anastomosis.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Sphenopalatine artery at the sphenopalatine foramen.

details.label: Course
details.value: Cross the roof of the nasal cavity on the anterior face of the sphenoid body to the septum, then run down and forward in a groove on the vomer to the incisive canal.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Septal twigs; anastomose with the greater palatine artery in the incisive canal, the septal branch of the superior labial artery and the anterior ethmoidal artery.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Posterior and inferior nasal septum; contribute to Kiesselbach plexus.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Run with the nasopalatine nerve.

name: Medial and lateral palpebral arteries (palpebral arterial arches)
function: Arteries of the eyelids, forming superior and inferior arterial arches between the ophthalmic and lacrimal arteries.

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Superior medial palpebral artery and inferior medial palpebral artery (from ophthalmic); superior lateral palpebral artery and inferior lateral palpebral artery (from lacrimal); joined as the superior and inferior palpebral arterial arches.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Medial palpebral arteries (superior and inferior) from the ophthalmic artery below the trochlea; lateral palpebral arteries (superior and inferior) from the lacrimal artery.

details.label: Course
details.value: Enter the lids at the medial and lateral angles and run toward each other between orbicularis oculi and the tarsal plates.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Superior and inferior palpebral arterial arches; twigs to conjunctiva and nasolacrimal duct; anastomoses with the angular, transverse facial, zygomatico-orbital and supraorbital arteries.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Eyelids, tarsal glands, palpebral conjunctiva.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Lie on the anterior surface of the tarsi deep to orbicularis oculi.

pearl: The lids are a meeting point of external and internal carotid territories, so they heal quickly and bleed freely.

name: Long medial striate artery (recurrent artery of Heubner)
function: Largest perforating branch of the anterior cerebral artery, supplying the anterior deep structures of the hemisphere.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Anterior cerebral artery at or just beyond the anterior communicating artery (proximal A2 or distal A1).

details.label: Course
details.value: Doubles back laterally along the A1 segment to enter the anterior perforated substance.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Perforating branches only.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Head of the caudate nucleus, anterior putamen and anterior limb of the internal capsule.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Runs above the A1 segment and optic nerve, close to the anterior communicating artery.

pearl: Occlusion, for example during clipping of an anterior communicating aneurysm, gives contralateral face and arm weakness with dysarthria.

name: Medial frontobasal (medial orbitofrontal) artery
function: First cortical branch of the anterior cerebral artery, supplying the medial orbital surface of the frontal lobe.

details.label: Origin
details.value: A2 segment of the anterior cerebral artery just beyond the anterior communicating artery.

details.label: Course
details.value: Runs forward along the gyrus rectus and medial orbital surface.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Cortical twigs.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Gyrus rectus, medial orbital gyri, olfactory bulb and tract.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Lies on the floor of the anterior cranial fossa beside the olfactory tract.

name: Callosomarginal artery
function: Major branch of the anterior cerebral artery running in the cingulate sulcus to the medial frontal lobe and paracentral lobule.

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Anterior medial frontal branch, intermediate medial frontal branch, posterior medial frontal branch, cingular branches, paracentral artery.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Anterior cerebral artery (A2) near the genu of the corpus callosum.

details.label: Course
details.value: Runs backward in the cingulate sulcus above the cingulate gyrus.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Anterior, intermediate and posterior medial frontal branches, cingular branches, paracentral artery.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Medial surface of the superior frontal gyrus, cingulate gyrus, and the paracentral lobule (leg and foot motor and sensory cortex).

details.label: Relations
details.value: Lies beside the falx cerebri, above the pericallosal artery.

pearl: Infarction of its paracentral territory causes contralateral leg weakness and sensory loss with urinary incontinence; subfalcine herniation can compress it against the falx.

name: Pericallosal artery
function: Continuation of the anterior cerebral artery over the corpus callosum to the medial parietal lobe.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Anterior cerebral artery beyond the origin of the callosomarginal artery.

details.label: Course
details.value: Runs backward in the callosal sulcus on the body of the corpus callosum toward the splenium.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Branches to the corpus callosum, precuneal artery, terminal cortical branches reaching the superolateral surface.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Corpus callosum (genu and body), cingulate gyrus, precuneus.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Lies under the free edge of the falx cerebri; anastomoses with the dorsal branch to corpus callosum of the posterior cerebral artery at the splenium.

name: Anterolateral central (lenticulostriate) arteries
function: Small end-arteries from the stem of the middle cerebral artery that supply the basal ganglia and internal capsule.

details.label: Origin
details.value: M1 segment of the middle cerebral artery (proximal medial and distal lateral groups).

details.label: Course
details.value: Ascend at right angles through the anterior perforated substance into the hemisphere.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Perforating end-arteries without significant anastomoses.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Putamen, globus pallidus, body of the caudate nucleus and the genu and posterior limb of the internal capsule.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Enter the brain lateral to the optic tract; the long medial striate artery enters medial to them.

pearl: Hypertensive lipohyalinosis and Charcot-Bouchard microaneurysms of these vessels cause lacunar infarcts (pure motor stroke) and putaminal hemorrhage.

name: Lateral frontobasal (lateral orbitofrontal) artery
function: Cortical branch of the middle cerebral artery to the lateral orbital surface and inferior frontal gyrus.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Middle cerebral artery (superior division) in the lateral sulcus.

details.label: Course
details.value: Runs forward and up over the lateral orbital surface of the frontal lobe.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Cortical twigs.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Lateral orbital gyri and the orbital part of the inferior frontal gyrus.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Emerges from the anterior ramus of the lateral sulcus.

name: Prefrontal artery
function: Cortical branch of the middle cerebral artery to the lateral prefrontal cortex.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Middle cerebral artery (superior division) in the lateral sulcus.

details.label: Course
details.value: Fans upward over the triangular and opercular parts of the inferior frontal gyrus and the middle frontal gyrus.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Cortical twigs.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Inferior and middle frontal gyri, including Broca's area in the dominant hemisphere and the frontal eye field.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Emerges from the lateral sulcus over the frontal operculum.

pearl: Occlusion in the dominant hemisphere produces Broca (nonfluent) aphasia; involvement of the frontal eye field deviates the eyes toward the lesion.

name: Artery of precentral sulcus
function: Cortical branch of the middle cerebral artery running in the precentral sulcus.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Middle cerebral artery (superior division) in the lateral sulcus.

details.label: Course
details.value: Ascends in the precentral sulcus.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Cortical twigs to the adjoining gyri.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Posterior parts of the middle and inferior frontal gyri and the lower precentral gyrus (premotor cortex and face and arm motor cortex).

details.label: Relations
details.value: Lies in front of the artery of the central sulcus.

name: Artery of central sulcus
function: Cortical branch of the middle cerebral artery running in the central sulcus to the primary motor and sensory cortex.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Middle cerebral artery (superior division) in the lateral sulcus.

details.label: Course
details.value: Ascends in the central sulcus toward the superior margin of the hemisphere.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Cortical twigs to the precentral and postcentral gyri.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Precentral and postcentral gyri for the face and upper limb.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Lies between the arteries of the precentral and postcentral sulci; its territory meets the anterior cerebral territory near the superior margin.

pearl: Occlusion causes contralateral weakness and sensory loss of the face and arm with relative sparing of the leg.

name: Artery of postcentral sulcus (anterior parietal artery)
function: Cortical branch of the middle cerebral artery running in the postcentral sulcus.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Middle cerebral artery in the lateral sulcus.

details.label: Course
details.value: Ascends in the postcentral sulcus and then back along the intraparietal sulcus.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Cortical twigs.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Postcentral gyrus (face and arm somatosensory cortex) and anterior part of the parietal lobules.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Lies behind the artery of the central sulcus.

name: Posterior parietal artery
function: Cortical branch of the middle cerebral artery to the posterior parietal lobe.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Middle cerebral artery (inferior or superior division) at the posterior end of the lateral sulcus.

details.label: Course
details.value: Emerges from the posterior ramus of the lateral sulcus and runs up and back over the supramarginal gyrus.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Cortical twigs.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Supramarginal gyrus and inferior and superior parietal lobules.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Lies between the artery of the postcentral sulcus and the artery to the angular gyrus.

pearl: Infarction of the non-dominant parietal lobe causes contralateral hemispatial neglect.

name: Artery to angular gyrus
function: Terminal cortical branch of the middle cerebral artery, supplying the angular gyrus.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Terminal part of the middle cerebral artery at the posterior end of the lateral sulcus.

details.label: Course
details.value: Runs back over the superior temporal gyrus to the angular gyrus.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Cortical twigs.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Angular gyrus and adjoining parts of the supramarginal gyrus and lateral occipital cortex.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Its territory borders the posterior cerebral territory in the posterior watershed zone.

pearl: Dominant angular gyrus infarction gives Gerstmann syndrome: agraphia, acalculia, finger agnosia and left-right disorientation.

name: Temporal branches of middle cerebral artery (anterior, middle and posterior)
function: Cortical branches of the inferior division of the middle cerebral artery, supplying the lateral temporal lobe.

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Polar temporal artery (temporal pole), anterior temporal artery, middle temporal artery, posterior temporal artery (continuing as the temporo-occipital branch).

details.label: Origin
details.value: Middle cerebral artery (inferior division) in the lateral sulcus.

details.label: Course
details.value: Descend out of the lateral sulcus over the superior and middle temporal gyri; the posterior branch continues toward the occipital lobe as the temporo-occipital branch.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Cortical twigs.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Temporal pole and the superior and middle temporal gyri, including the primary auditory cortex and Wernicke's area in the dominant hemisphere.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Emerge under the temporal operculum.

pearl: Dominant inferior-division occlusion causes Wernicke (fluent) aphasia, often with a contralateral superior quadrantanopia.

name: Thalamoperforating and thalamogeniculate arteries
function: Perforating branches of the posterior cerebral artery that supply the thalamus and upper midbrain.

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Thalamoperforating arteries (from P1, through the posterior perforated substance); thalamogeniculate arteries (from P2, to the posterolateral thalamus and geniculate bodies).

details.label: Origin
details.value: Thalamoperforating (posteromedial central) arteries from the P1 segment; thalamogeniculate arteries from the P2 segment.

details.label: Course
details.value: Thalamoperforating arteries enter the posterior perforated substance in the interpeduncular fossa; thalamogeniculate arteries enter the brain around the geniculate bodies.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Perforating end-arteries.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Medial and anterior thalamus, subthalamus and paramedian midbrain (thalamoperforating); ventral posterior and lateral thalamus and geniculate bodies (thalamogeniculate).

details.label: Relations
details.value: The oculomotor nerve emerges among the thalamoperforating vessels in the interpeduncular fossa.

pearl: Thalamogeniculate infarction causes contralateral hemisensory loss followed by thalamic pain (Dejerine-Roussy syndrome).

name: Posterior medial and posterior lateral choroidal arteries
