function: Branches of the posterior cerebral artery supplying the choroid plexuses of the third and lateral ventricles.

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Posterior medial choroidal artery (to choroid plexus of the 3rd ventricle); posterior lateral choroidal artery (to choroid plexus of the lateral ventricle).

details.label: Origin
details.value: P2 segment of the posterior cerebral artery.

details.label: Course
details.value: Posterior medial choroidal artery curves around the midbrain to the roof of the third ventricle; posterior lateral choroidal artery passes over the pulvinar through the choroidal fissure into the lateral ventricle.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Twigs to the tectum, pineal region, pulvinar, lateral geniculate body and fornix.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Choroid plexus of the third ventricle (medial); choroid plexus of the lateral ventricle, pulvinar and lateral geniculate body (lateral).

details.label: Relations
details.value: The posterior lateral choroidal artery anastomoses with the anterior choroidal artery in the choroid plexus of the lateral ventricle.

name: Medial occipital artery (parieto-occipital and calcarine branches)
function: Medial terminal division of the posterior cerebral artery, supplying the primary visual cortex.

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Dorsal branch to corpus callosum (posterior pericallosal artery), parieto-occipital branch (in the parieto-occipital sulcus), calcarine branch (in the calcarine sulcus), occipitotemporal branches.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Terminal division of the posterior cerebral artery behind the midbrain.

details.label: Course
details.value: Runs backward on the medial surface of the occipital lobe toward the calcarine and parieto-occipital sulci.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Dorsal branch to corpus callosum (posterior pericallosal artery), parieto-occipital branch, calcarine branch, occipitotemporal branches.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Splenium of the corpus callosum, cuneus, precuneus, lingual gyrus and the primary visual cortex on the banks of the calcarine sulcus.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Lies under the splenium beside the great cerebral vein and the free edge of the tentorium.

pearl: Occlusion gives contralateral homonymous hemianopia with macular sparing, because the occipital pole also receives middle cerebral collaterals.

name: Temporal branches of posterior cerebral artery (lateral occipital artery)
function: Lateral terminal division of the posterior cerebral artery, supplying the inferior surface of the temporal and occipital lobes.

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Anterior temporal artery, posterior temporal artery, occipitotemporal branches.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Terminal division of the posterior cerebral artery behind the midbrain.

details.label: Course
details.value: Run laterally and backward across the parahippocampal and occipitotemporal gyri on the tentorial surface of the hemisphere.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Anterior temporal artery, posterior temporal artery, occipitotemporal branches.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Uncus, hippocampus and parahippocampal gyrus, and the medial and lateral occipitotemporal (fusiform) gyri.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Lie on the tentorium cerebelli; the artery is compressed against the tentorial edge in uncal herniation.

pearl: Bilateral or dominant inferior temporal infarction causes memory impairment, and fusiform involvement causes prosopagnosia.

name: Pontine arteries
function: Numerous small branches of the basilar artery that supply the pons.

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Medial (paramedian) pontine branches; lateral (short and long circumferential) pontine branches.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Both sides of the basilar artery along the basilar sulcus.

details.label: Course
details.value: Paramedian (medial) branches enter the pons beside the midline; short and long circumferential (lateral) branches wind around its sides.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Perforating end-arteries.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Corticospinal and corticobulbar tracts, pontine nuclei, medial lemniscus, abducens nucleus and fibres, and the lateral pontine tegmentum.

details.label: Relations
details.value: The abducens nerve emerges at the lower border of the pons between them.

pearl: Bilateral paramedian pontine infarction from basilar thrombosis causes locked-in syndrome; lacunar occlusion of one perforator causes pure motor hemiparesis or ataxic hemiparesis.
